objects.title: Significant Cyber Threat Notification Process

objects.content: Financial entities maintain mechanisms that promptly detect anomalous activities, ICT network performance issues and ICT-related incidents, identify potential material single points of failure, and are regularly tested under Article 25.
objects.heading: Detection
objects.title: Promptly detect anomalous activity and material single points of failure

objects.content: Detection mechanisms provide multiple control layers, define alert thresholds and criteria that trigger ICT-related incident response, and automatically alert the relevant response staff.
objects.heading: Detection
objects.title: Use layered controls and response-triggering alerts

objects.content: Financial entities devote sufficient resources and capabilities to monitor user activity, ICT anomalies and ICT-related incidents, with particular attention to cyber-attacks.
objects.heading: Detection
objects.title: Resource monitoring of users, anomalies and incidents

objects.content: Financial entities other than microenterprises report to their competent authorities, upon request, an estimation of aggregated annual costs and losses caused by major ICT-related incidents.
objects.heading: Response and recovery
objects.title: Report aggregated annual major-incident costs and losses on request

objects.content: The European Supervisory Authorities, through the Joint Committee, develop common guidelines on estimating the aggregated annual costs and losses referred to in Article 11(10).
objects.heading: Response and recovery
objects.title: Establish common guidelines for annual incident cost and loss estimates

objects.content: Documented continuity arrangements enable rapid and effective resolution of all ICT-related incidents, immediate activation of suitable containment and recovery plans, preliminary impact, damage and loss estimation, and updated internal, external and regulatory communication.
objects.heading: Response and recovery
objects.title: Incident response, containment, impact and communication arrangements

objects.content: After a major ICT-related incident disrupts core activities, the financial entity reviews its causes and required improvements, assesses whether procedures were followed and actions were effective across alert response, impact and severity assessment, forensics where appropriate, escalation and communication, and, unless it is a microenterprise, communicates implemented changes to the competent authority on request.
objects.heading: Learning and evolving
objects.title: Review major incidents that disrupt core activities

objects.content: Lessons from real incidents and continuity or recovery challenges are continuously incorporated into ICT risk assessment and relevant framework reviews; incident trends and patterns are analysed, and senior ICT staff report the resulting findings and recommendations to the management body at least annually.
objects.heading: Learning and evolving
objects.title: Feed incident lessons into risk assessment and management reporting

objects.content: Financial entities maintain crisis communication plans for responsible disclosure of at least major ICT-related incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparts and the public as appropriate, implement internal and external communication policies that distinguish response staff from staff who need information, and assign at least one person to implement the incident communication strategy and public and media function.
objects.heading: Communication
objects.title: Maintain ICT crisis and stakeholder communication arrangements

objects.content: DORA Articles 5 to 15 do not apply to electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC; those entities follow the simplified ICT risk management framework in Article 16.
objects.heading: Simplified ICT risk management framework
objects.title: Exempted electronic money institutions use the simplified ICT framework

objects.content: The simplified ICT risk management framework is documented and reviewed periodically and upon a major ICT-related incident in compliance with supervisory instructions, continuously improved from implementation and monitoring lessons, and its review report is submitted to the competent authority on request.
objects.heading: Simplified ICT risk management framework
objects.title: Review and improve the simplified framework after a major incident

objects.content: Financial entities define, establish and implement a process to detect, manage and notify ICT-related incidents.
objects.heading: ICT-related incident management process
objects.title: Establish an ICT-related incident management process

objects.content: Financial entities record every ICT-related incident and significant cyber threat and use consistent, integrated monitoring, handling and follow-up procedures so root causes are identified, documented and addressed to prevent recurrence.
objects.heading: ICT-related incident management process
objects.title: Record incidents and threats and address root causes

objects.content: The incident management process uses early warning indicators and procedures to identify, track, log, categorise and classify ICT-related incidents by priority, severity and the criticality of affected services under Article 18(1).
objects.heading: ICT-related incident management process
objects.title: Establish early warning and incident classification procedures

objects.content: The incident management process assigns the roles and responsibilities activated for different ICT-related incident types and scenarios.
objects.heading: ICT-related incident management process
objects.title: Assign incident roles and responsibilities

objects.content: The incident management process covers staff, stakeholder and media communication, client notification, internal escalation including customer complaints, and counterpart information as appropriate; at least major incidents are reported to senior management and explained to the management body with their impact, response and additional controls.
objects.heading: ICT-related incident management process
objects.title: Plan incident communication and management escalation

objects.content: The incident management process establishes response procedures that mitigate impact and return services to an operational and secure state in a timely manner.
objects.heading: ICT-related incident management process
objects.title: Mitigate incident impacts and restore secure service

objects.content: Financial entities classify ICT-related incidents and determine their impact using affected clients, financial counterparts and transactions plus reputational impact; duration and downtime; geographical spread; data availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality losses; affected-service criticality; and direct and indirect economic impact.
objects.heading: Classification of ICT-related incidents and cyber threats
objects.title: Classify ICT incidents using six impact criteria

objects.content: Financial entities classify cyber threats as significant based on criticality of services, transactions and operations at risk, the number or relevance of targeted clients or financial counterparts, and the geographical spread of areas at risk.
objects.heading: Classification of ICT-related incidents and cyber threats
objects.title: Classify cyber threats using potential impact criteria

objects.content: Financial entities report major ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority, produce and submit the initial notification and reports after collecting and analysing relevant information using the Article 20 templates, use alternative notification means if technical impossibility prevents initial template submission, and include information needed to determine incident significance and possible cross-border impact.
objects.heading: Reporting of major ICT-related incidents and voluntary notification of significant cyber threats
objects.title: Report major incidents to the relevant competent authority

objects.content: A financial entity may voluntarily notify a significant cyber threat to its relevant competent authority when it considers the threat relevant to the financial system, service users or clients.
objects.heading: Reporting of major ICT-related incidents and voluntary notification of significant cyber threats
objects.title: Voluntarily notify a relevant significant cyber threat

objects.content: When a major ICT-related incident impacts clients' financial interests, the entity informs them without undue delay after becoming aware of it and explains mitigation measures; where applicable for a significant cyber threat, the entity informs potentially affected clients of appropriate protection measures they may take.
objects.heading: Reporting of major ICT-related incidents and voluntary notification of significant cyber threats
objects.title: Inform affected clients about major incidents and significant threats

objects.content: Within prescribed time limits, financial entities submit an initial notification; an intermediate report and further updates whenever incident status or handling changes significantly, relevant status information becomes available or the authority requests one; and a final report after root-cause analysis is complete and actual impact figures can replace estimates, regardless of mitigation implementation status.
objects.heading: Reporting of major ICT-related incidents and voluntary notification of significant cyber threats
objects.title: Submit initial, intermediate, updated and final incident reports

objects.content: A financial entity may outsource incident reporting in accordance with applicable Union and national sectoral law and remains fully responsible for fulfilling the reporting requirements.
objects.heading: Reporting of major ICT-related incidents and voluntary notification of significant cyber threats
objects.title: Retain responsibility when incident reporting is outsourced

objects.content: DORA applies to electronic money institutions, including electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC.
objects.heading: Scope
objects.title: DORA scope includes electronic money institutions

objects.content: Supervisory feedback does not transfer responsibility: the reporting financial entity remains fully responsible for handling the reported ICT-related incident and its consequences.
objects.heading: Supervisory feedback
objects.title: Retain incident handling responsibility after supervisory feedback

objects.content: DORA Chapter III requirements also apply to operational or security payment-related incidents and major operational or security payment-related incidents concerning electronic money institutions, including incidents that are not ICT-related under Article 3(9).
objects.heading: Operational or security payment-related incidents concerning specified financial entities
objects.title: Apply Chapter III to EMI payment-related incidents

objects.content: A major ICT-related incident is an ICT-related incident with a high adverse impact on the network and information systems supporting a critical or important function of the financial entity.
objects.heading: Definitions
objects.title: Definition of a major ICT-related incident

objects.content: A major operational or security payment-related incident is an operational or security payment-related incident with a high adverse impact on the payment-related services provided.
objects.heading: Definitions
objects.title: Definition of a major operational or security payment-related incident

objects.content: Cyber threat has the meaning assigned by Article 2(8) of Regulation (EU) 2019/881.
objects.heading: Definitions
objects.title: Definition of a cyber threat

objects.content: A significant cyber threat is a cyber threat whose technical characteristics indicate that it could result in a major ICT-related incident or a major operational or security payment-related incident.
objects.heading: Definitions
objects.title: Definition of a significant cyber threat

objects.content: An ICT-related incident is an unplanned single event or series of linked events that compromises network and information system security and adversely affects data availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality, or services provided by the financial entity.
objects.heading: Definitions
objects.title: Definition of an ICT-related incident

objects.content: An operational or security payment-related incident is an unplanned single event or series of linked events, whether ICT-related or not, that adversely affects payment-related data availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality, or payment-related services provided by an entity listed in Article 2(1)(a) to (d).
objects.heading: Definitions
objects.title: Definition of an operational or security payment-related incident

objects.content: The documented ICT risk management framework is reviewed at least annually, periodically for microenterprises, and upon a major ICT-related incident, supervisory instruction, or relevant testing or audit conclusion; it is continuously improved from implementation and monitoring lessons, and its review report is submitted to the competent authority on request.
objects.heading: ICT risk management framework
objects.title: Review the full ICT risk management framework after a major incident

objects.content: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 applies from 17 January 2025.
objects.heading: Entry into force and application
objects.title: DORA application date

objects.content: The ICT change management process is approved by appropriate lines of management and has specific protocols in place.
objects.heading: Protection and prevention
objects.title: Management approval and specific protocols for ICT change management

objects.content: Financial entities implement documented, risk-based ICT change management policies, procedures, and controls as part of overall change management so all ICT system changes are recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented, and verified in a controlled manner.
objects.heading: Protection and prevention
objects.title: Documented risk-based ICT change management

objects.content: Final fields cover incident and root-cause resolution status and timing, cause categories and detailed analysis, permanent corrective action, procedural changes, additional controls and lessons, timing differences, applicable resolution-authority impact, detailed economic impact, financial recoveries and recurring-incident information, with conditional mandatory rules and field formats.
objects.heading: Content of the final report
objects.title: Major-incident final template fields

objects.content: General and initial fields cover submission and entity identity, affected and aggregated entities, authority contacts, parent and currency information, entity and authority incident references, detection and major-classification timestamps, description, criteria and thresholds, impacted EEA states, discovery and origin, continuity-plan activation, reclassification and other relevant information, with stage-specific mandatory conditions and field formats.
objects.heading: Major-incident template, data glossary and instructions
objects.title: Major-incident general and initial template fields

objects.content: Intermediate fields cover occurrence and recovery timing, detailed classification impacts and thresholds, incident type and threat techniques, affected functions, processes, infrastructure and third parties, client financial-interest impact, notifications to other authorities, temporary recovery actions and applicable indicators of compromise, with conditional mandatory rules and field formats.
objects.heading: Content of the intermediate report
objects.title: Major-incident intermediate template fields

objects.content: The significant-cyber-threat template and glossary specify notifying-entity and contact information, detection and relevant timestamps, threat description, status, changes and potential impact, hypothetical major-incident classification criteria, prevention actions, other notifications, indicators of compromise and other available relevant information, with mandatory conditions and field formats.
objects.heading: Significant-cyber-threat template, data glossary and instructions
objects.title: Significant-cyber-threat notification fields and instructions

objects.content: Financial entities use Annex I for all three report stages, complete the fields required for each stage under Regulation (EU) 2025/301, ensure submitted information is complete and accurate, use estimates where possible when accurate initial or intermediate values are unavailable, resubmit all required and updated prior information with intermediate and final reports, and follow Annex II.
objects.heading: Template for reporting ICT-related major incidents
objects.title: Use the major-incident template by reporting stage

objects.content: A financial entity may submit two or all three reporting stages together when regular activities have recovered or root-cause analysis is complete and every applicable Regulation (EU) 2025/301 Article 5 deadline is met.
objects.heading: Joint submission of initial notification, intermediate and final reports
objects.title: Combine report stages when completion and deadlines permit

objects.content: Information about recurring non-major ICT-related incidents that cumulatively meet the conditions for one major incident under Regulation (EU) 2024/1772 Article 8(2) is provided in aggregated form.
objects.heading: Recurring ICT-related incidents
objects.title: Report collectively major recurring incidents in aggregated form

objects.content: Financial entities submit through secure electronic channels made available by the competent authority. If unable to use them, the entity informs the authority through another secure means agreed with it and, when required, resubmits through the authority channel once available.
objects.heading: Use of secure electronic channels
objects.title: Submit through the authority's secure electronic channel

objects.content: If further assessment shows that a reported major ICT-related incident never met the applicable criteria and thresholds, the financial entity notifies the competent authority of reclassification to non-major using the Annex II instructions for the report-type and other-information fields.
objects.heading: Reclassification of major ICT-related incidents
objects.title: Notify a major-to-non-major reclassification

objects.content: A financial entity informs its competent authority of a reporting outsourcing arrangement as soon as it is concluded and before the first outsourced submission, provides the third party's name, contact details and identification code, and informs the authority as soon as reporting is no longer outsourced.
objects.heading: Notification of outsourcing of the reporting obligations
objects.title: Notify the authority of a reporting outsourcing arrangement

objects.content: An outsourced reporting provider may aggregate one provider-originated major incident affecting multiple clients only when each affected entity classifies it as major, all covered entities are in one Member State under the same competent authority, and that authority has explicitly allowed aggregation for the entity type. Listed entity types must report individually, and any financial entity provides an individual report when the authority requests its impact.
objects.heading: Aggregated reporting
objects.title: Apply conditions for third-party aggregated reporting

objects.content: A financial entity choosing to notify a significant cyber threat uses Annex III, follows the Annex IV data glossary and instructions, and ensures the notification is complete and accurate.
objects.heading: Notification of significant cyber threats
objects.title: Use the significant-cyber-threat template accurately

objects.content: The template records the entity name and LEI, reference-year dates, currency, incident number, final-report submission date, incident reference, per-incident gross costs and losses and recoveries in thousands of currency units, and reference-year totals.
objects.heading: Reporting template for gross costs and losses and financial recoveries in a reference year

segments.value: Reporting template for gross costs and losses and financial recoveries in a reference year

objects.title: Annual incident cost and loss reporting template fields

objects.content: Financial entities aggregate costs and losses falling within the requested reference year, choose either a completed calendar year or a completed accounting year with finalised financial statements, apply that choice to future estimates, exclude amounts outside the reference year, and may change the choice after notifying the authority if it does not object within two months.
objects.heading: Provisions on the estimation of aggregated annual costs and losses of major ICT-related incidents
objects.title: Select and consistently apply a completed reference year

objects.content: The estimate includes every incident classified as major for which the entity submitted a final report in the reference year, plus any incident with a final report submitted in an earlier reference year that had a quantifiable financial impact in the current reference year.
objects.heading: Provisions on the estimation of aggregated annual costs and losses of major ICT-related incidents
objects.title: Include major incidents with financial impact in the reference year

objects.content: Financial entities estimate each included major incident separately to obtain gross costs and losses using the Regulation (EU) 2024/1772 Article 7 cost types, estimate financial recoveries using the Regulation (EU) 2025/302 Annex II specification, and aggregate gross costs and losses and recoveries across those incidents.
objects.heading: Provisions on the estimation of aggregated annual costs and losses of major ICT-related incidents
objects.title: Calculate gross costs, losses and financial recoveries sequentially

objects.content: The submitted estimate includes a breakdown of gross costs and losses and financial recoveries for each included major incident, uses the Annex template, and identifies each included incident or adjustment with the same institution incident reference used in the final incident report.
objects.heading: Provisions on the estimation of aggregated annual costs and losses of major ICT-related incidents
objects.title: Submit per-incident breakdowns with stable incident references

objects.content: Estimates use costs, losses, recoveries and accounting provisions reflected in the reference year's financial statements or applicable supervisory reporting; where accurate data is unavailable, other available information is used to the extent possible, and adjustments to an earlier year's submitted estimate are included in the reference year in which they are made.
objects.heading: Provisions on the estimation of aggregated annual costs and losses of major ICT-related incidents
objects.title: Use financial records and recognise later adjustments

objects.content: MFSA describes clear governance, segregation of duties, comprehensive records, impact assessment, pre-deployment testing, rollback and recovery, and a structured workflow as important elements of ICT change management.
objects.title: MFSA description of ICT change management lifecycle

objects.content: From 17 January 2025, MFSA Authorised Persons in DORA scope report major ICT-related incidents and may voluntarily notify significant cyber threats through the Cyber Reporting Management System within the Licence Holder Portal using the provided templates.
objects.heading: Cyber Reporting Management System

locator.label: Cyber Reporting Management System, DORA reporting paragraphs

objects.title: Use CRMS for Malta DORA incident and threat submissions

objects.content: For entities in DORA Article 2(1)(a)-(d), including electronic money institutions and exempted electronic money institutions, the prior PSD2 incident-reporting obligation ceases and DORA provides the reporting mechanism for operational or security payment-related incidents irrespective of their ICT nature.
objects.heading: Major ICT-Related Incidents

locator.label: Major ICT-Related Incidents, payment-related reporting transition

objects.title: Replace the prior PSD2 incident-reporting path with DORA

objects.content: MFSA Authorised Persons report every major ICT-related incident to the Authority through CRMS within the Licence Holder Portal using the provided template.
objects.heading: The Reporting Process
objects.title: Submit every major ICT incident to MFSA through CRMS

objects.content: The MFSA process does not replace or supersede an Authorised Person's legal obligation to notify incidents to other competent authorities unless DORA specifically supersedes that obligation.
objects.heading: The Reporting Process

locator.label: The Reporting Process, other notification obligations

objects.title: Preserve incident notifications owed to other authorities

objects.content: The MFSA process restates the initial-notification four-hour and 24-hour limits, the intermediate-report 72-hour limit and recovery update, and the final-report one-month limit, and directs Authorised Persons to Regulation (EU) 2025/301 Article 5 for the governing time-limit details.
objects.heading: The Reporting Process
objects.title: Follow the three MFSA major-incident report stages

objects.content: The MFSA major ICT-related incident reporting process applies mandatorily from 17 January 2025 to all MFSA Authorised Persons within DORA Article 2 scope; its application to other Authorised Persons is stated separately as an expectation.
objects.heading: Scope and Applicability
objects.title: Apply the MFSA major-incident process to DORA entities

objects.content: For material changes, MFSA encourages management oversight, role separation, detailed transition planning, asset and critical-function mapping, secure development, formal change control, tested failover and rollback, incident integration, third-party participation, early supervisory engagement, and evidence through testing and documentation.
objects.title: MFSA public expectations for material ICT changes

objects.content: The MFSA significant-cyber-threat process applies voluntarily to Authorised Persons inside and outside DORA scope, describes notification as highly encouraged, and provides a notification template and user guidelines.
objects.heading: Introduction
objects.title: Keep the MFSA significant-threat process voluntary

objects.content: Affected-client counts include users unable to use or adversely affected by the service and contractually covered third-party beneficiaries; affected-counterpart counts cover contractual financial counterparts; relevance considers business objectives and market efficiency; transaction counts and values include monetary transactions with at least one Union leg. Unavailable actual values are estimated from comparable reference periods.
objects.heading: Clients, financial counterparts and transactions
objects.title: Measure affected clients, counterparts and transactions

objects.content: A cyber threat is significant only when it could affect critical or important functions or specified external parties, has a high probability of materialisation based at least on relevant risks and exploitable vulnerabilities, known actor capability and intent, persistence and incident knowledge, and could meet the critical-services criterion, the clients-counterparts-transactions threshold or the geographical-spread threshold. Other materiality thresholds may also be considered when the threat type and available information support them.
objects.heading: High materiality thresholds for determining significant cyber threats
objects.title: Determine whether a cyber threat is significant

objects.content: Reputational impact exists when the incident is reflected in media, generates repetitive complaints from different clients or counterparts, causes or is likely to cause regulatory non-compliance, or causes or is likely to cause a material loss of clients or counterparts; the entity also considers actual or likely visibility for each condition.
objects.heading: Reputational impact
objects.title: Determine incident reputational impact

objects.content: Incident duration runs from occurrence to resolution, using detection time, earlier log evidence or estimates when necessary. Service downtime runs from full or partial unavailability to restoration of the previous service level, includes any resulting delayed service until fully provided, and uses detection time when its start cannot be determined.
objects.heading: Duration and service downtime
objects.title: Measure incident duration and service downtime

objects.content: Geographical spread considers actual or past impact in other Member States and its significance for clients and financial counterparts, branches or group financial entities, and, where information is available, financial market infrastructures or third-party providers that may affect financial entities they serve in other Member States.
objects.heading: Geographical spread
objects.title: Assess cross-border geographical spread

objects.content: Data-loss assessment considers temporary or permanent inaccessibility or unusability for availability, compromised source trustworthiness for authenticity, unauthorised modification causing inaccuracy or incompleteness for integrity, and unauthorised access or disclosure for confidentiality.
objects.heading: Data losses
objects.title: Assess availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality losses

objects.content: Critical services are affected when an incident affects ICT services or systems supporting critical or important functions, affects authorised, registered or supervised financial services, or constitutes successful malicious and unauthorised access to the entity's network and information systems.
objects.heading: Criticality of services affected
objects.title: Determine whether critical services are affected

objects.content: Economic impact sums incident-caused direct and indirect costs and losses without financial recoveries, including liable stolen assets, replacement or relocation, staff, contractual fees, customer redress, forgone revenue, communication and advisory costs. Day-to-day operation, post-incident business enhancement and insurance premium costs are excluded; available actual values or estimates are used at reporting time.
objects.heading: Economic impact
objects.title: Calculate direct and indirect incident costs and losses

objects.content: An incident is major for DORA Article 19(1) when it affects critical services under Article 6 and either meets the Article 9(5)(b) malicious unauthorised access threshold or meets at least two of the other materiality thresholds in Article 9(1) to (6).
objects.heading: Major incidents
objects.title: Determine whether an individual incident is major

objects.content: Non-major incidents are treated collectively as one major incident when they occur at least twice within six months, share the same apparent root cause and collectively meet Article 8(1). Financial entities assess recurrence monthly; this rule excludes microenterprises and DORA Article 16(1) entities.
objects.heading: Major incidents
objects.title: Assess recurring non-major incidents collectively each month

objects.content: This threshold is met if affected clients exceed 10 percent of clients using the affected service or 100,000 clients; affected financial counterparts exceed 30 percent of relevant counterparts; affected transaction count or value exceeds 10 percent of the related daily average; or a client or counterpart identified as relevant under Article 1(3) is affected. Unavailable actual values are estimated from comparable reference periods.
objects.heading: Materiality thresholds for determining major incidents
objects.title: Clients, counterparts and transactions materiality thresholds

objects.content: The reputational-impact threshold is met when any reputational-impact condition in Article 2(1)(a) to (d) is fulfilled.
objects.heading: Materiality thresholds for determining major incidents
objects.title: Reputational impact materiality threshold

objects.content: The duration and downtime threshold is met when incident duration exceeds 24 hours or service downtime exceeds two hours for an ICT service supporting a critical or important function.
objects.heading: Materiality thresholds for determining major incidents
objects.title: Duration and downtime materiality thresholds

objects.content: The geographical-spread threshold is met when the incident impacts two or more Member States as assessed under Article 4.
objects.heading: Materiality thresholds for determining major incidents
objects.title: Geographical spread materiality threshold

objects.content: The data-loss threshold is met when availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality impact has or will adversely affect business objectives or regulatory compliance, or when successful malicious and unauthorised access to network and information systems outside that condition may result in data loss.
objects.heading: Materiality thresholds for determining major incidents
objects.title: Data-loss materiality thresholds

objects.content: The economic-impact threshold is met when incident costs and losses have exceeded or are likely to exceed EUR 100,000.
objects.heading: Materiality thresholds for determining major incidents
objects.title: Economic impact materiality threshold

objects.content: Full-framework financial entities include the listed safeguards in ICT change management procedures for all changes to software, hardware, firmware components, systems, or security parameters.
objects.heading: ICT change management
objects.title: Scope of full-framework ICT change safeguards

objects.content: ICT change management procedures include verification of whether ICT security requirements have been met.
objects.title: Verify ICT security requirements

objects.content: ICT change management procedures include mechanisms that keep approval functions independent from functions responsible for requesting and implementing changes.
objects.title: Independent ICT change approval

objects.content: ICT change management procedures clearly describe roles and responsibilities that ensure changes are specified and planned, an adequate transition is designed, changes are tested and finalised in a controlled manner, and quality assurance is effective.
objects.title: Roles for planning, transition, controlled testing, and quality assurance

objects.content: Change details are documented and communicated, including purpose and scope, implementation timeline, and expected outcomes.
objects.title: Document and communicate change details

objects.content: ICT change management identifies fall-back procedures and responsibilities, including aborting changes and recovering from unsuccessfully implemented changes.
objects.title: Fall-back, abort, and recovery procedures

objects.content: Procedures, protocols, and tools manage emergency changes with adequate safeguards.
objects.title: Safeguards for emergency changes

objects.content: Procedures document, re-evaluate, assess, and approve emergency changes after implementation, including workarounds and patches.
objects.title: Post-implementation handling of emergency changes

objects.content: Financial entities identify the potential impact of a change on existing ICT security measures and assess whether additional ICT security measures are required.
objects.title: Assess impact on existing ICT security measures

objects.content: The full-framework incident policy documents the DORA Article 17 process, lists relevant internal and external ICT operations security contacts for cyber-threat monitoring, anomaly detection and vulnerability management, and establishes technical, organisational and operational mechanisms that support the process and prompt anomaly detection.
objects.heading: ICT-related incident management policy
objects.title: Document and support the full-framework incident policy

objects.content: The full-framework incident policy requires secure retention of all ICT-related incident evidence for no longer than necessary for its collection purpose, proportionate to the criticality of affected business functions, supporting processes and ICT and information assets, consistent with Regulation (EU) 2024/1772 Article 8(2) and applicable Union-law retention requirements.
objects.heading: ICT-related incident management policy
objects.title: Retain incident evidence securely for a justified period

objects.content: The full-framework incident policy establishes and implements mechanisms to analyse significant or recurring ICT-related incidents and patterns in incident number and occurrence.
objects.heading: ICT-related incident management policy
objects.title: Analyse significant and recurring incident patterns

objects.content: Full-framework entities assign clear detection and response roles; collect, monitor and analyse internal and external factors, logs, business and ICT information, user reports, cyber threats and relevant third-party provider incident notifications; and use alerting tools to detect anomalous activity at least for assets supporting critical or important functions.
objects.heading: Anomalous activities detection and criteria for ICT-related incidents detection and response
objects.title: Assign detection roles and monitor relevant anomaly inputs

objects.content: Full-framework entities prioritise anomaly alerts so detected incidents can be managed within entity-specified expected resolution times both inside and outside working hours, and automatically or manually record, analyse and evaluate relevant information about all anomalous activities and behaviours.
objects.heading: Anomalous activities detection and criteria for ICT-related incidents detection and response
objects.title: Prioritise anomaly alerts and evaluate anomaly information

objects.content: Full-framework entities protect anomalous activity records from tampering and unauthorised access at rest, in transit and where relevant in use, and log enough information to identify each anomaly's occurrence time, detection time and type.
objects.heading: Anomalous activities detection and criteria for ICT-related incidents detection and response
objects.title: Protect and time-stamp anomalous activity records

objects.content: Full-framework entities consider indications of malicious activity or compromise, losses of data availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality, adverse transaction or operational impact, ICT system or network unavailability, and the criticality of affected services when triggering incident detection and response processes.
objects.heading: Anomalous activities detection and criteria for ICT-related incidents detection and response
objects.title: Apply incident detection and response trigger criteria

objects.content: Simplified-framework entities identify and assess ICT and information security risks resulting from any major change in ICT systems, ICT services, processes, or procedures.
objects.heading: ICT risk management
objects.title: Assess ICT risk from major changes under the simplified framework

objects.content: A simplified-framework entity identifies and assesses ICT and information security risks after every major ICT-related incident.
objects.heading: ICT risk management
objects.title: Assess ICT risk after a major incident under the simplified framework

objects.content: A simplified-framework entity continuously monitors threats and vulnerabilities relevant to critical or important functions and their information and ICT assets, regularly reviews risk scenarios affecting those functions, and sets alert thresholds and criteria that trigger ICT-related incident response.
objects.heading: ICT risk management
objects.title: Monitor threats and set response triggers under the simplified framework

objects.content: For all ICT assets, a simplified-framework entity logs logical and physical access, ICT operations, system and network traffic, and ICT change events; monitors and analyses anomalous activity for critical or important ICT operations; monitors current cyber-threat information; and identifies information leakage, malicious code, other security threats, public vulnerabilities and corresponding updates. Log detail is aligned with its purpose and the producing asset's use.
objects.heading: ICT operations security
objects.title: Log and monitor security events under the simplified framework

objects.content: Simplified-framework entities establish and implement an ICT security testing plan that validates the effectiveness of ICT security measures, including measures under Articles 37 and 38, and considers identified threats and vulnerabilities.
objects.heading: ICT security testing
objects.title: Simplified-framework ICT security testing plan

objects.content: Simplified-framework entities ensure testing and approval of ICT systems before first use and before introducing changes to the production environment.
objects.heading: ICT systems acquisition, development, and maintenance
objects.title: Test and approve systems before production changes

objects.content: Simplified-framework entities develop, document, and implement an ICT change management procedure so all ICT system changes are recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented, and verified in a controlled manner with adequate safeguards for digital operational resilience.
objects.heading: ICT project and change management
objects.title: Simplified-framework controlled ICT change procedure

objects.content: When a simplified-framework review was initiated following ICT-related incidents, its review report describes that reason and lists every such incident with the related root-cause analysis.
objects.heading: Format and content of the report on the review of the simplified ICT risk management framework
objects.title: Include incident and root-cause details in a simplified-framework review report

objects.content: Every report stage identifies the submission type, affected financial entity and LEI, entity submitting and its identification code, aggregated entities where applicable, authority-contact persons, parent undertaking where applicable, and currency used for monetary impact.
objects.heading: General information to be provided in initial notifications and intermediate and final reports on major ICT-related incidents
objects.title: Provide general information in every incident report stage

objects.content: An initial notification provides at least the institution's incident reference, detection and classification timestamps, incident description, major-classification criteria, impacted Member States, discovery method, available origin information, business continuity plan activation, applicable major-to-non-major reclassification information and any other available relevant information.
objects.heading: Specific information to be provided in initial notifications
objects.title: Provide initial-notification incident information

objects.content: An intermediate report provides at least the authority incident reference where applicable, occurrence and regular-activity recovery timestamps, fulfilled major-classification criteria, incident type, applicable threat-actor techniques, affected functions, processes and infrastructure, client financial-interest impact, reports to other authorities, temporary recovery actions and applicable indicators of compromise.
objects.heading: Specific information to be provided in intermediate reports
objects.title: Provide intermediate-report incident information

objects.content: A final report provides incident root causes, incident-resolution and root-cause-address timestamps, resolution information, applicable resolution-authority information, direct and indirect costs and losses plus financial recoveries, and applicable recurring-incident information.
objects.heading: Specific information to be provided in final reports
objects.title: Provide final-report cause, resolution and loss information

objects.content: The initial notification is submitted as early as possible, no later than four hours after classification as major, and no later than 24 hours after the entity became aware of the ICT-related incident.
objects.heading: Time limits for the initial notification, and for the intermediate and final reports
objects.title: Submit the initial notification within both time limits

objects.content: The intermediate report is submitted no later than 72 hours after the initial notification even without a status or handling change; an updated intermediate report is submitted without undue delay and in every case when regular activities recover.
objects.heading: Time limits for the initial notification, and for the intermediate and final reports
objects.title: Submit and update the intermediate report within prescribed times

objects.content: The final report is submitted no later than one month after the intermediate report or, where applicable, the latest updated intermediate report.
objects.heading: Time limits for the initial notification, and for the intermediate and final reports
objects.title: Submit the final report within one month

objects.content: When an incident is classified as major more than 24 hours after awareness, the initial notification is submitted within four hours after that major classification.
objects.heading: Time limits for the initial notification, and for the intermediate and final reports
objects.title: Apply the four-hour limit after a late major classification

objects.content: An entity unable to submit a notification or report within its deadline informs the competent authority without undue delay and no later than that deadline and explains the delay.
objects.heading: Time limits for the initial notification, and for the intermediate and final reports
objects.title: Notify and explain an inability to meet a reporting deadline

objects.content: A deadline falling on a weekend or bank holiday in the reporting entity's Member State may move to noon on the next working day. This extension does not apply to initial or intermediate reports by listed entities or financial entities identified as NIS2 essential or important, and a competent authority may prospectively remove it for other significant or systemically important financial entities after notification.
objects.heading: Time limits for the initial notification, and for the intermediate and final reports
objects.title: Apply the conditional weekend and bank-holiday extension

objects.content: A voluntary significant-cyber-threat notification contains notifying-entity information, detection and other relevant timestamps, threat description and potential impact, classification criteria that would trigger a major report if materialised, threat status and changes, applicable prevention actions and indicators of compromise, notifications to other entities or authorities, and other available relevant information.
objects.heading: Content of the voluntary notification of significant cyber threats
objects.title: Provide prescribed significant-cyber-threat notification content

conditions: The institution was covered by an aggregated major-incident notification or report.
The competent authority requests an individual notification or report about the impact on the institution.

objects.statement: When the competent authority requests information about an institution-specific impact after an aggregated major-incident submission, an electronic money institution shall provide an individual notification or report.
objects.title: Provide an individual impact report after an aggregated submission

conditions: The institution has submitted an intermediate report for a major ICT-related incident.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution shall submit the final report no later than one month after the intermediate report or, where an updated intermediate report was submitted, no later than one month after the latest updated intermediate report.
objects.title: Submit the final report within one month

conditions: An amount in a previously submitted annual estimate is adjusted in the current reference year.
exclusions: Microenterprises and electronic money institutions using the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution should include an adjustment to costs or losses from a previously submitted annual estimate in the estimate for the reference year in which the adjustment is made.
objects.title: Recognise earlier-estimate adjustments in the current reference year

conditions: The institution is estimating costs, losses or recoveries for the requested reference year.
exclusions: Microenterprises and electronic money institutions using the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution should base annual incident cost, loss and recovery estimates on amounts and accounting provisions reflected in its financial statements or applicable supervisory reporting for the reference year, using other available data and information to the extent possible when accurate values are unavailable.
objects.title: Base estimates on financial or supervisory records

conditions: The incident belongs to the requested reference-year population.
exclusions: Microenterprises and electronic money institutions using the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: For each included major incident, an electronic money institution should estimate gross costs and losses using the prescribed cost types, estimate financial recoveries separately, and then aggregate gross costs and losses and recoveries across all included incidents.
objects.title: Estimate and aggregate gross amounts and recoveries sequentially

conditions: The competent authority has requested an annual estimate under DORA Article 11(10).
exclusions: Incidents never classified as major.
Incidents with no financial impact falling within the reference year.
Microenterprises and electronic money institutions using the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: A requested annual estimate should include every incident classified as major for which the institution submitted a final report in the reference year and every incident with a final report submitted in an earlier reference year that had a quantifiable financial impact in the current reference year.
objects.title: Include every major incident with reference-year financial impact

conditions: The competent authority has requested an annual estimate under DORA Article 11(10).
exclusions: Microenterprises.
Electronic money institutions using the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: For requested annual cost and loss estimates, a non-microenterprise electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework should select either the completed calendar year or its completed accounting year with finalised financial statements, apply that basis consistently to future estimates and exclude costs and losses falling outside the selected reference year.
objects.title: Use one completed reference-year basis consistently

conditions: The institution previously selected a calendar-year or accounting-year basis.
The institution notified the competent authority of the proposed change.
The competent authority did not object within two months after receiving the notification.
exclusions: Microenterprises.
Electronic money institutions using the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: A non-microenterprise electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework may change its annual cost and loss reference-year basis after notifying the competent authority, provided that the authority does not object within two months after receiving the notification.
objects.title: Change the reference-year basis only after notice and non-objection

conditions: The competent authority has requested an annual estimate under DORA Article 11(10).
exclusions: Microenterprises and electronic money institutions using the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution should use the Joint Guidelines Annex template to submit reference-year totals and a per-incident breakdown of gross costs and losses and financial recoveries, identifying each item with the same incident reference used in its final incident report.
objects.title: Submit annual totals and per-incident cost and recovery details

conditions: The competent authority has requested the estimate.
exclusions: Microenterprises.
Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: Upon a competent authority's request, a non-microenterprise electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall report an estimate of its aggregated annual costs and losses caused by major ICT-related incidents.
objects.title: Report annual major-incident costs and losses on request

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: Senior ICT staff of an electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall report incident-derived ICT risk assessment findings and recommendations to the management body at least annually.
objects.title: Report incident-derived findings to the management body annually

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall protect anomaly records from tampering and unauthorised access at rest, in transit and where relevant in use, and shall log the occurrence time, detection time and type of each detected anomaly.
objects.title: Protect anomaly records and capture required timestamps and type

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall use mechanisms that keep change approval functions independent from functions responsible for requesting and implementing changes.
objects.title: Keep ICT change approval independent

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall implement documented, risk-based ICT change management policies, procedures, and controls as part of overall change management so every ICT system change is recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented, and verified in a controlled manner.
objects.title: Operate a documented and controlled ICT change lifecycle

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall document and communicate each change's purpose and scope, implementation timeline, and expected outcomes.
objects.title: Document and communicate change details

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall identify fall-back procedures and responsibilities, including arrangements for aborting changes and recovering from changes that were not implemented successfully.
objects.title: Define change fall-back, abort, and recovery arrangements

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall have its ICT change management process approved by appropriate lines of management.
objects.title: Obtain appropriate management approval for the change process

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall clearly describe roles and responsibilities that ensure changes are specified and planned, an adequate transition is designed, changes are tested and finalised in a controlled manner, and quality assurance is effective.
objects.title: Assign roles for planning, transition, testing, and quality assurance

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall identify each change's potential impact on existing ICT security measures and assess whether additional ICT security measures are required.
objects.title: Assess change impact on ICT security measures

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall include verification that ICT security requirements have been met for every change to software, hardware, firmware components, systems, or security parameters.
objects.title: Verify ICT security requirements for every change

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall maintain specific protocols for its ICT change management process.
objects.title: Maintain specific ICT change protocols

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall maintain crisis communication plans and internal and external communication policies for responsible disclosure of at least major ICT-related incidents or vulnerabilities as appropriate, distinguish response staff from staff who need information, and assign at least one person to implement the incident communication strategy and public and media function.
objects.title: Maintain crisis and stakeholder communication arrangements

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall document, re-evaluate, assess, and approve emergency changes after implementation, including workarounds and patches.
objects.title: Review and approve emergency changes after implementation

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall maintain procedures, protocols, and tools that manage emergency changes with adequate safeguards.
objects.title: Apply adequate safeguards to emergency changes

conditions: A major ICT-related incident has occurred.
exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: After a major ICT-related incident, an electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall review the documented framework, continuously improve it from implementation and monitoring lessons, and submit the review report to the competent authority on request.
objects.title: Review and improve the full framework after a major incident

exclusions: Alert thresholds and expected resolution times are defined by the institution.
Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall implement layered detection controls with defined response-triggering thresholds, automatically alert responsible staff, and prioritise alerts so incidents can be managed within institution-defined expected resolution times inside and outside working hours.
objects.title: Trigger, alert and prioritise incident response

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall assign clear detection and response roles and operate regularly tested mechanisms with sufficient resources that promptly detect anomalies, network performance issues, ICT-related incidents and potential material single points of failure by monitoring relevant logs, business and ICT information, user reports, cyber threats and third-party provider incident notifications, with alerting tools covering at least assets supporting critical or important functions.
objects.title: Detect anomalies and incidents from relevant monitoring inputs

exclusions: The source does not prescribe one universal retention duration.
Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall retain all ICT-related incident evidence securely for no longer than necessary for its collection purpose, using a period proportionate to affected-function, process and asset criticality and consistent with recurring-incident assessment and applicable Union-law retention requirements.
objects.title: Retain ICT incident evidence securely for a justified period

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall continuously incorporate lessons from real incidents and continuity or recovery challenges into ICT risk assessment and relevant framework reviews and shall analyse incident frequency, type, magnitude, evolution and patterns over time.
objects.title: Incorporate incident lessons into ICT risk assessment

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall document its ICT-related incident management process in an incident policy, maintain relevant internal and external ICT operations security contacts, and operate technical, organisational and operational mechanisms that support the process and prompt anomaly detection.
objects.title: Maintain a documented and supported ICT incident policy

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall maintain documented arrangements that rapidly resolve every ICT-related incident, immediately activate suitable containment and recovery plans, estimate preliminary impact, damage and loss, and provide updated internal, external and regulatory communication.
objects.title: Maintain documented incident response and recovery arrangements

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall consider indications of malicious activity or compromise, data losses across availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality, adverse transaction or operational impact, ICT system or network unavailability, and affected-service criticality when triggering incident detection and response.
objects.title: Consider all prescribed incident response trigger criteria

conditions: A major ICT-related incident has disrupted core activities.
exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: After a major ICT-related incident disrupts core activities, an electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall review the disruption causes and required improvements and assess procedure adherence and action effectiveness across alert response, impact and severity assessment, forensics where appropriate, escalation and communication.
objects.title: Review a major incident that disrupted core activities

exclusions: Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC use the simplified ICT risk management branch.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall operate mechanisms that analyse significant or recurring ICT-related incidents and patterns in their number and occurrence.
objects.title: Analyse significant and recurring incident patterns

conditions: An ICT-related incident is being classified or reclassified as information changes.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution shall classify each ICT-related incident and determine its impact by applying the prescribed calculation methods for affected clients, financial counterparts and transactions, reputational impact, duration and service downtime, geographical spread, data losses, affected-service criticality and economic impact, using permitted estimates where actual values cannot yet be determined.
objects.title: Assess every prescribed ICT incident classification criterion

objects.statement: An electronic money institution shall maintain incident communication, client-notification, counterpart-information and internal-escalation arrangements and shall report at least major ICT-related incidents to senior management and explain their impact, response and resulting additional controls to the management body.
objects.title: Plan incident communication and management escalation

objects.statement: An electronic money institution shall use early warning indicators and procedures that identify, track, log, categorise and classify ICT-related incidents by priority, severity and affected-service criticality under the DORA classification criteria.
objects.title: Use early warning and classify ICT-related incidents

objects.statement: An electronic money institution shall define, establish and implement a process that detects, manages and notifies ICT-related incidents.
objects.title: Operate an ICT-related incident management process

objects.statement: An electronic money institution shall record every ICT-related incident and significant cyber threat and operate consistent, integrated monitoring, handling and follow-up procedures that identify, document and address root causes to prevent recurrence.
objects.title: Record incidents and threats and complete root-cause follow-up

objects.statement: An electronic money institution shall establish ICT-related incident response procedures that mitigate impact and return affected services to an operational and secure state in a timely manner.
objects.title: Mitigate incident impact and restore secure service

objects.statement: An electronic money institution shall assign the roles and responsibilities activated for each relevant ICT-related incident type and scenario.
objects.title: Assign roles for incident types and scenarios

conditions: The incident is classified as major no later than 24 hours after the institution became aware of it.

objects.statement: When an ICT-related incident is classified as major no later than 24 hours after awareness, an electronic money institution shall submit the initial notification as early as possible, no later than four hours after classification and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of the incident.
objects.title: Meet both initial-notification time limits

conditions: The institution has submitted an initial notification for a major ICT-related incident.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution shall submit an intermediate report no later than 72 hours after the initial notification even if incident status or handling has not changed, and shall submit an updated intermediate report without undue delay after prescribed changes or requests and in every case when regular activities have recovered.
objects.title: Submit and update the intermediate report on time

conditions: Regular activities have recovered or root-cause analysis is complete.
Every deadline for the report stages submitted together is met.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution may submit two or all three major-incident report stages together only when regular activities have recovered or root-cause analysis is complete and every deadline applicable to the combined stages is met.
objects.title: Combine report stages only when completion and deadlines permit

conditions: The incident is classified as major more than 24 hours after the institution became aware of it.

objects.statement: When an ICT-related incident is classified as major more than 24 hours after the electronic money institution became aware of it, the institution shall submit the initial notification within four hours after classification.
objects.title: Report within four hours after a late major classification

conditions: The ICT-related incident has been classified as major under the applicable criteria and thresholds.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution shall report every ICT-related incident classified as major to its relevant competent authority, submit the prescribed initial notification and reports with information sufficient to assess significance and possible cross-border impact, and use alternative notification means when technical impossibility prevents submission of the initial-notification template.
objects.title: Report every major ICT-related incident

conditions: A major ICT-related incident affects clients' financial interests.

objects.statement: As soon as it becomes aware that a major ICT-related incident affects clients' financial interests, an electronic money institution shall inform those clients without undue delay and explain the measures taken to mitigate the adverse effects.
objects.title: Notify clients whose financial interests are affected

conditions: The institution has completed the prescribed classification-criterion assessment for the incident.
exclusions: Institution-defined severity levels do not replace the statutory major-incident combination rule.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution shall treat an ICT-related incident as major when it affects a critical service and either involves successful malicious and unauthorised system access that may result in data loss or meets at least two of the other prescribed client, counterpart, transaction, reputation, duration, downtime, geographical, data-loss or economic-impact materiality thresholds.
objects.title: Apply the DORA major-incident combination rule

conditions: The institution is preparing a final report for a major ICT-related incident.

objects.statement: In a final report, an electronic money institution shall provide the prescribed incident-resolution and root-cause information, permanent corrective actions, procedural and control changes, lessons learned, applicable resolution-authority impact, direct and indirect costs and losses, financial recoveries and recurring-incident information, following the template's field conditions and formats.
objects.title: Complete the required final-report fields

conditions: The institution is preparing an initial notification for a major ICT-related incident.

objects.statement: In an initial notification, an electronic money institution shall provide the prescribed incident reference, detection and major-classification times, description, classification criteria, impacted Member States, discovery method, available origin information, business-continuity activation, applicable reclassification information and other available relevant information, following the template's field conditions and formats.
objects.title: Complete the required initial-notification fields

conditions: The institution is preparing an intermediate report or updated intermediate report for a major ICT-related incident.

objects.statement: In an intermediate report, an electronic money institution shall provide the prescribed occurrence and recovery times, classification impacts and thresholds, incident type and applicable threat techniques, affected functions, processes, infrastructure and third parties, client financial-interest impact, other authority notifications, temporary recovery actions and applicable indicators of compromise, following the template's field conditions and formats.
objects.title: Complete the required intermediate-report fields

conditions: The incident was reported as major.
Further assessment establishes that it never met the applicable major-incident criteria and thresholds.

objects.statement: If further assessment concludes that a previously reported ICT-related incident never met the major-incident criteria and thresholds, an electronic money institution shall notify the competent authority that it has reclassified the incident as non-major using the prescribed report-type and other-information fields.
objects.title: Notify the authority of a major-to-non-major reclassification

conditions: The institution is preparing an initial notification, intermediate report or final report for a major ICT-related incident.

objects.statement: At every major-incident reporting stage, an electronic money institution shall use the prescribed template and instructions and provide complete and accurate general information identifying the submission, affected institution, submitting entity, any entities covered by an aggregated report, authority contacts, applicable parent undertaking and reporting currency.
objects.title: Provide the required general information at every report stage

conditions: The institution is reporting an ICT-related incident classified as major.

objects.statement: For a reportable major ICT-related incident, an electronic money institution shall submit an initial notification, an intermediate report and further updates when prescribed, and a final report after root-cause analysis is complete and actual impact figures are available to replace estimates, regardless of whether mitigation measures have been fully implemented.
objects.title: Maintain the major-incident report sequence

conditions: The institution is submitting a major-incident notification or report.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution shall submit major-incident notifications and reports through the competent authority's secure electronic channel; if it cannot use that channel, it shall inform the authority through another secure means agreed with the authority and, when required, resubmit through the authority channel once available.
objects.title: Use the competent authority's secure reporting channel

conditions: The institution is an MFSA Authorised Person within DORA scope.
The ICT-related incident has been classified as major.
exclusions: This requirement does not establish a submission route for a non-ICT operational or security payment-related incident.

objects.statement: An MFSA Authorised Person that is an electronic money institution shall submit every major ICT-related incident notification and report to the MFSA through CRMS within the Licence Holder Portal using the provided template.
objects.title: Submit Malta major ICT incident reports through CRMS

conditions: A separate legal obligation requires the institution to notify the incident to another competent authority.
exclusions: An obligation specifically superseded by DORA.

objects.statement: An MFSA Authorised Person that is an electronic money institution shall continue to meet any incident-notification obligation owed to another competent authority unless DORA specifically supersedes that obligation.
objects.title: Preserve Malta incident notifications owed to other authorities

conditions: The institution is an MFSA Authorised Person.
The cyber threat has been classified as significant.
The institution has chosen to make the voluntary notification.
exclusions: MFSA encouragement does not change the voluntary nature of the notification decision.

objects.statement: When an MFSA Authorised Person that is an electronic money institution chooses to notify a significant cyber threat, it shall submit the notification to the MFSA through CRMS within the Licence Holder Portal using the provided template.
objects.title: Submit a chosen Malta significant-threat notification through CRMS

conditions: Incident reporting is outsourced or supervisory feedback has been received.
exclusions: Outsourcing or supervisory feedback does not transfer the institution's responsibility.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution may outsource incident reporting in accordance with applicable Union and national sectoral law, and shall remain fully responsible for meeting its reporting requirements and for handling the incident and its consequences, including after supervisory feedback.
objects.title: Retain responsibility for outsourced reporting and incident handling

conditions: The event is an operational or security incident affecting payment-related services.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution shall apply the DORA Chapter III incident-management, classification and reporting requirements to its operational or security payment-related incidents and major operational or security payment-related incidents, including incidents that are not ICT-related.
objects.title: Apply DORA Chapter III to EMI payment-related incidents

exclusions: Microenterprises.
Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC.

objects.statement: Each month, a non-microenterprise electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall determine whether incidents that were individually non-major occurred at least twice within six months, share the same apparent root cause and collectively meet the major-incident rule, in which case it shall treat them as one major incident.
objects.title: Assess recurring non-major incidents collectively each month

conditions: Recurring non-major incidents cumulatively meet the Regulation (EU) 2024/1772 Article 8(2) conditions for one major incident.
exclusions: Microenterprises.
Electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC.
