objects.statement: A non-microenterprise electronic money institution using the full ICT risk management framework shall provide information in aggregated form when recurring incidents that were individually non-major cumulatively meet the prescribed conditions for one major ICT-related incident.
objects.title: Report collectively major recurring incidents in aggregated form

conditions: The institution cannot meet an applicable major-incident reporting deadline.

objects.statement: If an electronic money institution cannot submit an initial notification, intermediate report or final report within its applicable time limit, it shall inform the competent authority without undue delay and no later than that time limit and explain the reasons for the delay.
objects.title: Notify and explain a reporting delay by the deadline

conditions: The institution has concluded or ended an arrangement that outsources major-incident reporting.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution that outsources major-incident reporting shall inform its competent authority as soon as the arrangement is concluded and before the first outsourced submission, provide the reporting third party's name, contact details and identification code, and inform the authority as soon as the arrangement ends.
objects.title: Notify the authority when reporting is outsourced or resumed internally

conditions: A cyber threat is being assessed using information available to the institution.
exclusions: Classification as significant does not by itself decide whether the institution will make a voluntary notification.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution shall classify a cyber threat as significant only when it could affect critical or important functions or specified external parties, has a high probability of materialisation after considering the prescribed risk, vulnerability, threat-actor, persistence and incident-history factors, and could meet the critical-services criterion, the clients-counterparts-transactions threshold or the geographical-spread threshold.
objects.title: Apply all significant-cyber-threat classification conditions

conditions: The cyber threat has been classified as significant.
Clients could be affected and protection measures are applicable.

objects.statement: Where applicable, an electronic money institution shall inform clients potentially affected by a significant cyber threat of appropriate protection measures they may take.
objects.title: Give potentially affected clients threat-protection information

conditions: The cyber threat has been classified as significant.
The institution has chosen to make the voluntary notification.

objects.statement: When choosing to notify a significant cyber threat, an electronic money institution shall use the prescribed template and instructions and provide complete and accurate entity, contact, timing, threat-description, status, change, potential-impact, hypothetical major-classification, prevention-action, other-notification, indicator-of-compromise and other available relevant information.
objects.title: Complete the significant-cyber-threat notification accurately

conditions: The cyber threat has been classified as significant.
The institution considers the threat relevant to the financial system, service users or clients.
exclusions: Classification as significant does not make regulatory notification mandatory.

objects.statement: An electronic money institution may voluntarily notify its relevant competent authority of a significant cyber threat when it considers the threat relevant to the financial system, service users or clients.
objects.title: Voluntarily notify a relevant significant cyber threat

objects.statement: An exempted electronic money institution using the simplified ICT risk management framework shall develop, document, and implement an ICT change management procedure so every ICT system change is recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented, and verified in a controlled manner with adequate safeguards for digital operational resilience.
objects.title: Operate a controlled ICT change procedure under the simplified framework

objects.statement: An exempted electronic money institution using the simplified ICT risk management framework shall establish and implement an ICT security testing plan that validates the effectiveness of ICT security measures under Articles 37 and 38 and considers threats and vulnerabilities identified through its simplified ICT risk management framework.
objects.title: Cover change controls in the ICT security testing plan

conditions: A major ICT-related incident has occurred.

objects.statement: After a major ICT-related incident, an exempted electronic money institution using the simplified ICT risk management framework shall review the documented framework in compliance with supervisory instructions, continuously improve it from implementation and monitoring lessons, and submit the review report to the competent authority on request.
objects.title: Review and improve the simplified framework after a major incident

exclusions: The source leaves the alert threshold values to the institution.

objects.statement: An exempted electronic money institution using the simplified ICT risk management framework shall set alert thresholds and criteria that trigger and initiate ICT-related incident response processes.
objects.title: Set incident response alert thresholds and criteria

conditions: The framework review was initiated following one or more ICT-related incidents.

objects.statement: When an ICT risk management framework review was initiated following ICT-related incidents, an exempted electronic money institution using the simplified framework shall state that reason in the review report and list every such incident with its related root-cause analysis.
objects.title: Include incidents and root causes in an incident-triggered review report

conditions: A major ICT-related incident has occurred.

objects.statement: An exempted electronic money institution using the simplified ICT risk management framework shall identify and assess ICT and information security risks after every major ICT-related incident.
objects.title: Assess ICT risk after every major incident

conditions: The change is a major change in an ICT system, ICT service, process, or procedure.

objects.statement: An exempted electronic money institution using the simplified ICT risk management framework shall identify and assess ICT and information security risks resulting from any major change in ICT systems, ICT services, processes, or procedures.
objects.title: Assess ICT risk arising from major changes

objects.statement: An exempted electronic money institution using the simplified ICT risk management framework shall test and approve ICT systems before introducing changes to the production environment.
objects.title: Test and approve ICT systems before production changes

objects.statement: For every ICT asset, an exempted electronic money institution using the simplified ICT risk management framework shall log logical and physical access, ICT operations, system and network traffic, and ICT change events at a level of detail aligned with the log purpose and use of the producing asset.
objects.title: Log access, operations, traffic and change events

objects.statement: An exempted electronic money institution using the simplified ICT risk management framework shall monitor and analyse anomalous activity for critical or important ICT operations, monitor current cyber-threat information, and identify information leakage, malicious code, other security threats, public software and hardware vulnerabilities and corresponding updates.
objects.title: Monitor anomalies, threats, leakage, malware and vulnerabilities

objects.statement: An exempted electronic money institution using the simplified ICT risk management framework shall continuously monitor threats and vulnerabilities relevant to critical or important functions and their information and ICT assets and regularly review risk scenarios affecting those functions.
objects.title: Monitor relevant threats and vulnerabilities continuously

conditions: Major-incident reporting has been outsourced to a third-party service provider.
Every aggregation condition in Regulation (EU) 2025/302 Article 7 is met.

objects.statement: An outsourced reporting provider may submit one aggregated notification or report for a provider-originated or provider-caused major ICT-related incident affecting multiple financial entities only when it provides the relevant ICT service to multiple entities or a group, each covered entity classifies the incident as major, all covered entities are in one Member State and supervised by the same competent authority, and that authority explicitly permits aggregation for the entity type.
objects.title: Permit third-party aggregated reporting only under all conditions

conditions: The applicable deadline falls on a weekend or bank holiday in the reporting institution's Member State.
exclusions: The extension does not apply to an initial notification or intermediate report by an institution identified as an essential or important entity under Directive (EU) 2022/2555.
The extension does not apply to an initial notification or intermediate report where the competent authority has prospectively removed it for the institution and notified that decision.

objects.statement: When a major-incident reporting deadline falls on a weekend or bank holiday in its Member State, an electronic money institution may submit by noon on the next working day, subject to the prescribed exclusions for initial and intermediate reports and any prospective competent-authority decision notified to the institution.
objects.title: Apply the conditional weekend and bank-holiday extension

assumptions: Final incident reports and finance or supervisory records can be reconciled through stable incident references.
objects.conclusion: Gate the workflow on request and applicability, use one approved completed reference-year basis, reconcile the full incident population, calculate gross amounts and recoveries separately, and preserve source-level and per-incident traceability.
conditions: The workflow applies only after a competent-authority request to an applicable non-microenterprise EMI using the full framework.
The institution approves its reference-year basis, financial data sources, authority route, roles, and retention.
objects.question: Which reusable engineering pattern should prepare an authority-requested annual major-incident cost and loss estimate?
objects.rationale: This pattern converts the Joint Guidelines sequence into deterministic population, calculation, reconciliation, and report checks while leaving institution financial systems and the selected reference-year basis configurable.
objects.title: Engineering baseline for annual incident cost and loss estimates

assumptions: The institution operates a system capable of maintaining stable change identifiers, lifecycle states, approvals, and audit history.
objects.conclusion: Use a management-approved process, a stable change identity, explicit lifecycle gates, named responsibilities, and required planning and communication fields.
conditions: Each institution maps the generic roles and workflow gates to its approved organisation and systems before use.
objects.question: Which reusable control pattern should the public engineering baseline use for ICT change governance, lifecycle gates, planning, and records?
objects.rationale: The pattern converts source requirements into deterministic workflow and record checks while leaving institution-specific roles and systems configurable.
objects.title: Public engineering baseline for governed ICT change workflow

assumptions: Current legal criteria and thresholds are available to the institution's classification process in a controlled form.
objects.conclusion: Use versioned criteria assessments, immutable reassessment history, evidence-linked root-cause and effectiveness reviews, monthly recurring-incident grouping, and at least annual management-body reporting.
conditions: Internal severity labels may support operations but cannot replace DORA classification criteria or materiality thresholds.
Review ownership, completion targets, systems, and evidence retention require institution approval.
objects.question: Which reusable engineering pattern should support classification, recurring analysis, post-incident review, and management learning?
objects.rationale: The pattern keeps legal thresholds distinct from internal severity measures and creates reproducible links from incident facts to classification, improvements, risks, and governance decisions.
objects.title: Engineering baseline for incident classification and learning

assumptions: An institution maps the generic owner roles and process interfaces to authorised functions before operational use.
objects.conclusion: Use one stable incident case, explicit scope and role routing, protected chronology, monitored trigger inputs, controlled response and secure-restoration gates, and traceable communication outcomes.
conditions: Statutory scope and conditions remain governed by the referenced Requirements and Provisions.
Internal targets, systems, channels, access rules, and retention schedules require institution approval.
objects.question: Which reusable engineering pattern should govern incident intake, monitoring, response, recovery, records, and communications?
objects.rationale: This pattern connects event detection to action and evidence while preserving institution-specific systems, roles, alert thresholds, internal targets, communication channels, and retention schedules as configuration.
objects.title: Engineering baseline for governed incident operations

assumptions: The institution can resume direct reporting if the delegated route fails.
objects.conclusion: Preserve EMI accountability, gate third-party access on authority notice, evaluate every aggregation condition explicitly, retain constituent links, and support institution-specific follow-up reports.
conditions: Contracts, third parties, competent-authority permissions, and operational access require institution approval.
objects.question: Which reusable engineering pattern should govern reporting delegation and aggregation?
objects.rationale: Delegation and aggregation alter execution and packaging but do not remove the institution's responsibility or the need to evidence each eligibility condition and individual impact.
objects.title: Engineering baseline for outsourced and aggregated reporting

assumptions: The institution maintains reliable awareness, classification, submission, recovery, and root-cause timestamps.
objects.conclusion: Separate mandatory triggers from voluntary decisions, calculate statutory deadlines from preserved timestamps, validate versioned report packages before release, require authorised human submission, and retain secure delivery evidence.
conditions: External submission requires an authorised institution role and never follows solely from an Agent recommendation.
Current authority routes, access roles, calendars, templates, and secure fallbacks require institution maintenance.
objects.question: Which reusable engineering pattern should control mandatory and voluntary reporting from classification through authority receipt?
objects.rationale: The pattern makes deadlines and content machine-checkable while keeping authority selection, voluntary notification, submission authority, and external side effects under institution-controlled roles and channels.
objects.title: Engineering baseline for regulatory incident reporting

assumptions: The institution can restrict emergency-path access and record all emergency actions.
objects.conclusion: Require owned fall-back and recovery arrangements, restricted emergency-path access, a complete audit trail, and time-bound post-implementation review and approval.
conditions: The institution defines the permitted post-implementation review period and fall-back test-depth rule before operational use.
objects.question: Which reusable control pattern should the public engineering baseline use for failed implementations and emergency changes?
objects.rationale: The pattern supports controlled recovery and emergency execution while leaving test depth and the retrospective review deadline to institution approval.
objects.title: Public engineering baseline for fall-back and emergency changes

assumptions: The institution can identify actors consistently across change, approval, deployment, and audit records.
objects.conclusion: Use traceable requirement-to-test mapping, risk-based test depth, deterministic identity comparison for conflicting roles, and a recorded security-control impact assessment.
conditions: The institution defines approved test-depth and major-change rules before operational use.
objects.question: Which reusable control pattern should the public engineering baseline use for security verification, role independence, and change risk assessment?
objects.rationale: These controls create repeatable pass and fail conditions and preserve institution-level choices for test depth, major-change criteria, and system mapping.
objects.title: Public engineering baseline for security gates and approval independence

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Keep applicability or request scope unresolved, prohibit unsupported submission, and escalate to the authorised regulatory liaison.
implementation_rules.statement: Initiate the report only for a competent-authority request addressed to a non-microenterprise EMI using the full ICT risk management framework, and record the request scope, due date, and submission route.

conditions: The applicability and request gate is satisfied.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Stop calculation, reconcile the period and financial-statement status, and obtain approval of the consistent basis.
implementation_rules.statement: Use either the completed calendar year or completed accounting year with finalised financial statements, apply the selected basis consistently, and exclude amounts outside that reference year.

conditions: The institution proposes to change its reference-year basis.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Continue using the existing basis and escalate any unapproved change.
implementation_rules.statement: Change the selected reference-year basis only after notifying the competent authority and recording that it did not object within two months after receipt.

conditions: The applicability and request gate is satisfied.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Reconcile the population against final reports and financial records before calculation continues.
implementation_rules.statement: Include every major incident with a final report in the reference year and every earlier-final-reported major incident with a quantifiable financial impact in the current reference year, using the final-report incident reference.

conditions: The included incident population is complete.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Reject netted or unreconciled calculations and repeat the prescribed sequence.
implementation_rules.statement: For each included incident, calculate gross costs and losses using the prescribed cost types, calculate financial recoveries separately, and aggregate gross amounts and recoveries across all included incidents without netting the two populations.

conditions: The applicability and request gate is satisfied.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Mark unsupported values, reconcile them to an approved data basis, and prevent report release until differences are explained.
implementation_rules.statement: Base values on financial statements or applicable supervisory reporting and their accounting provisions, identify estimates that use other available data, and include earlier-estimate adjustments in the reference year when the adjustment is made.

conditions: The annual estimate is prepared for submission.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Block release, complete or reconcile the missing totals, details, and incident references, and repeat quality review.
implementation_rules.statement: Use the Joint Guidelines Annex to report reference-year totals and per-incident gross costs and losses and recoveries, linked by the incident reference used in each final report.

objects.objective: A competent-authority request produces a complete, reconciled, and consistently prepared annual estimate of major-incident gross costs and losses and financial recoveries for an applicable EMI.
objects.title: Estimate and report annual major-incident costs and losses
objects.trigger_or_frequency: On a competent-authority request, supported by preparation after each selected reference year closes

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Block implementation when a required fall-back or recovery plan is missing or infeasible.
implementation_rules.statement: Define abort criteria, fall-back steps, recovery steps, responsible roles, required backups, decision authority, and verification of restored service for the change.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Escalate failed results, remediate the plan, and repeat verification before implementation.
implementation_rules.statement: Test or otherwise verify the fall-back and recovery arrangements at a depth determined by the institution's risk and criticality rules.

objects.objective: Every in-scope change has owned, feasible, and tested arrangements to abort implementation or recover when implementation is unsuccessful.
objects.title: Prepare and verify change fall-back and recovery
objects.trigger_or_frequency: Before production implementation and when the fall-back design changes

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Prevent the revised process from becoming effective and escalate to the ICT change governance owner.
implementation_rules.statement: Record approval of the ICT change management process by the institution's authorised management role before the process becomes effective.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Suspend use of an incomplete protocol and open a governance remediation item.
implementation_rules.statement: Maintain approved protocols covering change intake, classification, assessment, approval, implementation, verification, exceptions, and closure.

objects.objective: The ICT change management process has recorded management approval, named ownership, and specific protocols before it is used.
objects.title: Govern and approve the ICT change management process
objects.trigger_or_frequency: When the ICT change management process is established or materially revised

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Reject lifecycle actions that do not reference a valid change identifier.
implementation_rules.statement: Assign one stable identifier to the change and retain its scope, classification, affected assets, decisions, timestamps, and lifecycle status in a traceable record.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Block the transition, record the failed gate, and notify the change owner.
implementation_rules.statement: Prevent implementation until required assessment, testing, and approval gates pass, then require post-implementation verification before closure.

objects.objective: Every ICT change has one traceable record and cannot move through assessment, approval, implementation, verification, and closure without satisfying the required gates.
objects.title: Enforce the controlled ICT change lifecycle
objects.trigger_or_frequency: For every ICT change from registration through closure

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Return the change to planning and prevent implementation approval.
implementation_rules.statement: Require named accountable roles and documented specification, implementation plan, transition design, testing approach, and quality assurance before approval.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Hold implementation until required details are complete and communication is recorded.
implementation_rules.statement: Record and communicate purpose, scope, implementation timeline, and expected outcomes to the roles affected by the change.

objects.objective: Each change record names responsible roles and contains an approved plan, transition approach, quality assurance, purpose, scope, timeline, and expected outcomes.
objects.title: Record change responsibilities, plans, and expected outcomes
objects.trigger_or_frequency: During change planning and before implementation approval

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Block approval, retain the failed attempt in the audit trail, and notify the change management owner.
implementation_rules.statement: Compare approver identity with requester and implementer identities and reject the approval when the approver holds either conflicting role for the same change.

objects.objective: No actor approves an ICT change for which the same actor is recorded as requester or implementer.
objects.title: Enforce independence of ICT change approval
objects.trigger_or_frequency: At every ICT change approval action

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Prevent approval until unresolved impacts have an authorised treatment decision.
implementation_rules.statement: Identify affected ICT security measures, evaluate whether their effectiveness changes, and record any additional measures required before implementation.

conditions: The change is assessed under the simplified ICT risk management framework.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Treat an unclassified change as requiring assessment or escalate to the ICT risk owner.
implementation_rules.statement: Apply the institution's approved major-change criteria and complete an ICT and information security risk assessment for changes classified as major.

objects.objective: Each change has a recorded assessment of affected ICT security measures, additional safeguards, and, for simplified-framework major changes, resulting ICT and information security risks.
objects.title: Assess change risk and impact on ICT security controls
objects.trigger_or_frequency: During assessment of every change and again when scope materially changes

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Block approval until the mapping and missing test evidence are completed.
implementation_rules.statement: Map applicable ICT security requirements and identified threats and vulnerabilities to test cases and acceptance results for the change.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Apply the institution's highest required test depth or escalate for an authorised decision.
implementation_rules.statement: Select test depth using the institution's approved risk and criticality rules and record the resulting test scope.

objects.objective: A production change proceeds only after applicable ICT security requirements are mapped, tested at an appropriate depth, and approved with recorded results.
objects.title: Gate production changes on security requirements and testing
objects.trigger_or_frequency: Before each change is approved for production implementation

conditions: The normal change path cannot meet the documented operational need.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Deny emergency-path use or escalate immediately to the emergency change authority.
implementation_rules.statement: Restrict emergency-path access, require a recorded justification and authorised emergency approval, preserve an audit trail, and apply all safeguards that remain feasible before implementation.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Escalate overdue review, restrict further emergency access where appropriate, and track remediation to closure.
implementation_rules.statement: After implementation, document the final change, re-evaluate and assess its effects, complete the omitted controls, and obtain retrospective approval within the authorised period.

objects.objective: Emergency changes use restricted safeguards during implementation and complete documented re-evaluation, assessment, and approval within the institution's authorised period.
objects.title: Control emergency changes before and after implementation
objects.trigger_or_frequency: For every emergency change

conditions: The case is an ICT-related incident.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Keep the classification open, state unavailable inputs, and apply conservative escalation until the required criteria can be assessed.
implementation_rules.statement: Assess affected clients, financial counterparts and transactions, reputational impact, duration and downtime, geographical spread, data losses, affected-service criticality, and economic impact using the current prescribed methods, and label every estimated value.

conditions: The case is an ICT-related incident.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Reject an unsupported conclusion, retain the previous reportability state, and require reassessment by the classification owner.
implementation_rules.statement: Classify an ICT-related incident as major only through the prescribed critical-service condition and malicious-access or multi-threshold combination rule, using the current legal thresholds without substituting internal severity thresholds.

conditions: The case concerns a cyber threat that has not materialised as an incident.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Reject the significant-threat classification until all prescribed conditions are evidenced.
implementation_rules.statement: Classify a cyber threat as significant only after recording the potentially affected functions or parties, high-probability factors, and the applicable hypothetical materiality condition prescribed for significant cyber threats.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Treat the classification as unverified and prevent closure until a complete history is restored.
implementation_rules.statement: Record assessment inputs, calculation results, source-rule version, assessor, timestamps, conclusion, and every reassessment without overwriting prior conclusions.

objects.objective: Every in-scope event has a repeatable, versioned assessment of all prescribed criteria and a traceable conclusion on major-incident or significant-cyber-threat status.
objects.title: Classify incidents and significant cyber threats
objects.trigger_or_frequency: At initial triage and whenever new information may change a classification conclusion

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Use the emergency escalation route, record the missed target, and notify the communication owner.
implementation_rules.statement: Escalate incidents through approved severity and criticality paths; report at least every major ICT-related incident to senior management and provide the management body with impact, response, and resulting control information.

conditions: The full ICT risk management framework applies.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Restrict unapproved external communication and escalate to the crisis owner.
implementation_rules.statement: Maintain approved internal and external crisis communication plans, distinguish active response staff from information recipients, and assign an authorised person for incident communication and public or media functions.

conditions: A major ICT-related incident affects client financial interests.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Escalate the overdue notification, use an approved fallback channel, and record affected clients and corrective action.
implementation_rules.statement: Notify clients without undue delay when a major ICT-related incident affects their financial interests, identify the adverse effect, and explain mitigation measures taken.

conditions: The case is classified as a significant cyber threat and client protection information is applicable.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Escalate the missing protection information and prevent communication closure until addressed.
implementation_rules.statement: Where applicable, provide potentially affected clients with actionable protection measures for a significant cyber threat and record the applicability assessment.

conditions: The institution is subject to an external notification obligation that DORA has not superseded.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Escalate the missed or uncertain obligation to the authorised regulatory liaison and preserve the assessment record.
implementation_rules.statement: Evaluate every case against the institution's current external notification register and complete each Malta or other competent-authority notification that remains applicable alongside DORA.

objects.objective: Incident information reaches authorised internal decision-makers, affected clients, external stakeholders, and every separately competent authority through approved, timely, and traceable communication paths.
objects.title: Coordinate incident escalation and stakeholder communications
objects.trigger_or_frequency: When escalation, client impact, crisis communication, or an external notification obligation is triggered

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Record the monitoring gap, apply compensating detection, and escalate uncovered critical or important assets immediately.
implementation_rules.statement: Monitor relevant ICT and business information, security and performance logs, user reports, current cyber-threat information, public vulnerabilities, and third-party incident notifications, with explicit coverage of assets supporting critical or important functions.

conditions: The simplified ICT risk management framework applies.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Flag the asset as lacking required telemetry and apply approved compensating monitoring until logging is restored.
implementation_rules.statement: For each ICT asset in the simplified-framework scope, log logical and physical access, ICT operations, system and network traffic, and ICT change events at detail aligned with the log purpose and asset use.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Trigger manual triage when required input is unavailable or the automated decision is inconclusive.
implementation_rules.statement: Evaluate malicious activity or compromise, data availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality loss, transaction or operational impact, system or network unavailability, and affected-service criticality when deciding whether to trigger response.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Create a highest-priority manual alert, notify the monitoring owner, and preserve the unprocessed indicator for investigation.
implementation_rules.statement: Apply approved alert thresholds, notify responsible staff automatically, and assign initial category, priority, severity, and affected-service criticality so the response can operate inside and outside working hours.

objects.objective: Relevant monitoring inputs and early-warning indicators produce timely, traceable, prioritised alerts and initiate the applicable incident response process.
objects.title: Detect, log, triage, and alert on incident indicators
objects.trigger_or_frequency: Continuous monitoring with regular mechanism tests and immediate processing of generated alerts

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Create or reconcile the missing case immediately, preserve the original detection time, and escalate the intake failure.
implementation_rules.statement: Route every ICT-related incident, significant cyber threat, and operational or security payment-related incident, including a non-ICT payment incident, into the governed incident process and assign one stable case identifier.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Escalate to the governance owner and prevent case closure until ownership and contacts are recorded.
implementation_rules.statement: Maintain an approved incident policy, scenario-specific responsibility map, and current internal and external ICT operations security contacts; record the roles activated for each case.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Restrict access, preserve available source records, open an integrity investigation, and reconstruct the chronology under approval.
implementation_rules.statement: Preserve a tamper-evident chronology containing occurrence time, detection time, event type, material decisions, status changes, actions, evidence links, and root-cause follow-up, with protection against unauthorised access at rest, in transit, and where relevant in use.

conditions: The full ICT risk management framework applies.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Suspend deletion for the affected case, notify the record owner, and resolve the schedule or legal-hold conflict before disposal.
implementation_rules.statement: Apply an approved retention schedule that keeps incident evidence securely only as long as necessary, proportionate to affected-function, process, and asset criticality, while supporting recurring-incident assessment and applicable Union-law obligations.

objects.objective: Every in-scope ICT incident, significant cyber threat, and payment-related operational or security incident enters one governed process with named ownership, a protected record, root-cause follow-up, and justified evidence retention.
objects.title: Govern incident scope, ownership, records, and evidence
objects.trigger_or_frequency: When an in-scope event or threat is detected and throughout its lifecycle

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Escalate to crisis management, apply the safest available containment, and document unavailable or ineffective arrangements.
implementation_rules.statement: Select and activate approved containment and recovery arrangements according to incident type, severity, affected-service criticality, and current evidence, while recording decisions and timestamps.

conditions: The full ICT risk management framework applies.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Mark the estimate incomplete, state the missing inputs, and continue collection under the response owner.
implementation_rules.statement: Establish a preliminary impact, damage, and loss estimate and update it as reliable facts become available, keeping estimates distinguishable from actual values.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Keep the service restricted or invoke an approved degraded mode, record the failed criterion, and continue recovery.
implementation_rules.statement: Return an affected service to normal operation only after confirming service functionality, security, data integrity, and any required temporary risk treatment.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Escalate stale or conflicting status information and prevent unsupported closure or external reporting.
implementation_rules.statement: Provide current response, impact, recovery, and residual-risk information to the communication and regulatory-reporting controls whenever material facts change.

objects.objective: Each incident activates suitable containment and recovery arrangements, limits impact, maintains current impact estimates, and returns affected services to a verified operational and secure state.
objects.title: Contain incidents and restore services securely
objects.trigger_or_frequency: For every incident from response activation until secure service restoration

conditions: The institution is not a microenterprise and the full ICT risk management framework applies.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Complete the overdue assessment immediately, preserve the original due date, and trigger reporting assessment for any collectively major result.
implementation_rules.statement: Each month, identify individually non-major incidents occurring at least twice within six months with the same apparent root cause, aggregate their prescribed classification inputs, and apply the major-incident combination rule.

conditions: The full ICT risk management framework applies.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Record the analysis gap and require completion before the next management report.
implementation_rules.statement: Analyse significant and recurring incidents by number, occurrence, frequency, type, magnitude, evolution, and pattern, and link supported findings to risks and corrective actions.

conditions: The full ICT risk management framework applies.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Escalate an overdue or incomplete report and schedule a replacement management-body review.
implementation_rules.statement: Senior ICT staff shall report incident-derived ICT risk findings, trends, unresolved issues, and recommendations to the management body at least annually and retain the resulting decisions.

objects.objective: Recurring and significant incident patterns are assessed on schedule, collectively reclassified when required, and reflected in at least annual findings and recommendations to the management body.
objects.title: Analyse recurring incidents and report findings to management
objects.trigger_or_frequency: Monthly for recurring-incident assessment and at least annually for management-body reporting

conditions: Any incident reporting task is outsourced.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Suspend the affected delegated action, assume direct control where necessary, and remediate the accountability gap.
implementation_rules.statement: Keep the EMI responsible for report completeness, accuracy, deadlines, authority communications, incident handling, consequences, and supervisory feedback when any reporting task is performed by a third party.

conditions: Major-incident reporting is outsourced or returned to the institution.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Prevent the third party's first or further submission, notify the authority, and escalate the process breach.
implementation_rules.statement: Notify the competent authority as soon as a reporting outsourcing arrangement is concluded and before its first submission, include the third party's name, contacts, and identification code, and notify the authority as soon as the arrangement ends.

conditions: A third party proposes one submission for multiple institutions.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Reject aggregation and require separate institution submissions.
implementation_rules.statement: Permit a third party to aggregate incident reports only when it provides the relevant service, every covered institution classified the event as major, all institutions are in one Member State under the same competent authority, and that authority permits aggregation for the entity type.

conditions: A monthly recurring-incident assessment concludes that a group is collectively major.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Keep the reporting case open, correct the population or links, and do not submit an unsupported aggregate.
implementation_rules.statement: When recurring individually non-major incidents are collectively classified as one major incident, prepare the prescribed information in aggregated form and link every constituent incident.

conditions: The competent authority requests an institution-specific impact report.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Escalate the request, preserve its deadline, and provide a corrected individual report through the approved channel.
implementation_rules.statement: After an aggregated submission, produce an institution-specific notification or report when the competent authority requests information about the EMI's individual impact.

objects.objective: Outsourced and aggregated reporting proceeds only under the prescribed conditions, leaves the EMI fully accountable, and supports authority-requested institution-specific reports.
objects.title: Govern outsourced and aggregated incident reporting
objects.trigger_or_frequency: When reporting is outsourced, resumed internally, proposed in aggregated form, or followed by an authority request

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Keep corrective actions and the incident review open, escalate overdue analysis, and record unresolved evidence gaps.
implementation_rules.statement: Identify and document root causes, disruption causes, procedure adherence, and the effectiveness of alert response, impact and severity assessment, forensics where appropriate, escalation, communication, containment, and recovery.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Reject review closure until findings have an approved treatment, owner, due date, and target risk or control record.
implementation_rules.statement: Convert supported findings into owned improvements and incorporate relevant incident frequency, type, magnitude, evolution, patterns, and recovery challenges into ICT risk assessments and framework reviews.

conditions: The full ICT risk management framework applies.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Escalate the missing review to the ICT risk management owner and track completion.
implementation_rules.statement: After a major ICT-related incident, review and improve the full ICT risk management framework and retain a report suitable for submission to the competent authority on request.

conditions: The simplified ICT risk management framework applies.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Escalate the missing risk assessment or review content and keep the framework review open.
implementation_rules.statement: After a major ICT-related incident, identify and assess ICT and information security risks, review and improve the simplified framework under supervisory instructions, and list the triggering incidents and related root-cause analyses in the review report.

objects.objective: Every applicable major incident produces a complete root-cause and effectiveness review, updates risks and controls, and supports the required full- or simplified-framework review record.
objects.title: Complete post-incident review and apply lessons
objects.trigger_or_frequency: After every major incident and after any other incident selected by the approved review criteria

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Prevent submission with an unverified template and obtain the current official version.
implementation_rules.statement: Use the current template and instructions obtained from the applicable official channel and record the source location, retrieval time, version or label, and SHA-256 digest used for the submission.

conditions: The package contains an initial notification.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Block release, identify missing or inconsistent fields, and return the package to the reporting owner.
implementation_rules.statement: For each applicable stage, validate the prescribed general entity and submission fields and the initial-notification incident reference, times, description, criteria, Member States, discovery, origin, continuity, reclassification, and other available information.

conditions: The package contains an intermediate report or update.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Block release, identify missing or inconsistent fields, and return the package to the reporting owner.
implementation_rules.statement: Validate occurrence and recovery times, criterion impacts and thresholds, incident and threat details, affected functions and infrastructure, third parties, client financial interests, other authority notifications, recovery actions, and applicable indicators of compromise.

conditions: The package contains a final report.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Block release, identify missing or inconsistent fields, and return the package to the reporting owner.
implementation_rules.statement: Validate resolution and root cause, permanent corrections, procedure and control changes, lessons, resolution-authority impact where applicable, direct and indirect costs and losses, recoveries, and recurring-incident details.

conditions: An authorised decision selected voluntary significant-threat notification.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Block release, identify missing or inconsistent fields, and return the notification to the reporting owner.
implementation_rules.statement: For a chosen voluntary notification, validate entity, contact, timing, threat description and status, changes, potential impacts, hypothetical major classification, prevention action, other notifications, indicators of compromise, and other available relevant information.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Prevent release of inconsistent content and preserve both the rejected and corrected package versions.
implementation_rules.statement: Reconcile identifiers, timestamps, classifications, currency, impacts, and totals across stages; label estimates and unavailable fields according to the template; replace estimates with actual values when they become available without erasing prior submissions.

objects.objective: Every incident report stage and chosen significant-threat notification uses the current prescribed template and contains complete, accurate, internally consistent, and properly qualified information.
objects.title: Validate regulatory report content and templates
objects.trigger_or_frequency: Before every incident report stage or significant-threat notification is authorised for submission

conditions: The case is reportable as a major ICT-related incident.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Block an invalid stage transition, preserve the pending deadline, and escalate to the reporting owner.
implementation_rules.statement: Maintain initial notification, intermediate report and prescribed updates, and final report as ordered stages; issue the final report after root-cause analysis is complete and actual impact values are available, regardless of whether every mitigation action is complete.

conditions: The case is reportable as a major ICT-related incident.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Trigger the delay-notification path before the applicable deadline and escalate immediately.
implementation_rules.statement: Submit the initial notification as early as possible and, when classification occurs within 24 hours after awareness, by both four hours after classification and 24 hours after awareness; when classification occurs later, submit within four hours after classification.

conditions: The case is reportable as a major ICT-related incident.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Trigger the delay-notification path before the applicable deadline and escalate immediately.
implementation_rules.statement: Submit the intermediate report within 72 hours after the initial notification, update it without undue delay after prescribed changes or requests and whenever regular activities recover, and submit the final report within one month after the latest intermediate report.

conditions: A reporting deadline is at risk of being missed.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Use the approved escalation and secure fallback route, record the breach, and prioritise completion of the overdue report.
implementation_rules.statement: When a reporting stage cannot be submitted on time, inform the competent authority without undue delay and no later than the missed stage deadline, explain the reason, and retain the revised delivery plan.

conditions: The reporting owner proposes a combined-stage submission.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Reject the combined submission and continue with the earliest currently due stage.
implementation_rules.statement: Permit two or three reporting stages in one submission only when regular activities have recovered or root-cause analysis is complete and every deadline applicable to the combined stages is met.

conditions: A calculated deadline falls on a weekend or bank holiday in the institution's Member State.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Use the unextended deadline when eligibility cannot be demonstrated and escalate any delivery risk.
implementation_rules.statement: Apply a next-working-day noon extension only after checking the Member State calendar, prescribed initial- and intermediate-report exclusions, entity conditions, and any prospective competent-authority decision notified to the institution.

conditions: A previously reported incident is reassessed as never having met the major criteria.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Keep the reporting case open and escalate until the authority is notified through the prescribed path.
implementation_rules.statement: When later assessment shows the incident never met the major criteria and thresholds, submit the prescribed major-to-non-major reclassification notification and retain the assessment history and authority response.

objects.objective: Each major-incident reporting case follows the prescribed stage sequence, deadlines, update triggers, delay procedure, permitted extensions, and reclassification path using a traceable deadline ledger.
objects.title: Control regulatory report stages and deadlines
objects.trigger_or_frequency: From major classification until final report or accepted reclassification

conditions: The incident is classified as a major ICT-related incident.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Escalate immediately to the regulatory reporting owner, start a manually controlled reporting case, and preserve all original timestamps.
implementation_rules.statement: On a verified major ICT-related incident classification, create the mandatory reporting workflow immediately, identify the relevant competent authority, preserve the classification time, and initiate the initial-notification deadline without waiting for an optional business approval.

conditions: The case is an operational or security payment-related incident.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Keep reportability open, prohibit automatic submission, and escalate route confirmation to the authorised regulatory liaison.
implementation_rules.statement: Route operational or security payment-related incidents within EMI scope, including non-ICT incidents, through the applicable Chapter III classification and reporting assessment using the current authority route for that event type.

conditions: The case is classified as a significant cyber threat.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Do not submit a voluntary notification, preserve the pending assessment, and escalate to the authorised decision role.
implementation_rules.statement: For a verified significant cyber threat, record whether the threat is relevant to the financial system, service users, or clients and obtain an authorised decision before creating or closing a voluntary-notification workflow.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Prevent external submission until linkage is complete and internally consistent.
implementation_rules.statement: Link every reporting or voluntary-notification workflow to the incident or threat case, classification revision, applicable authority, trigger, decision basis, and deadline ledger.

objects.objective: A verified major-incident classification initiates mandatory reporting without an optional approval gate, while a significant-cyber-threat notification proceeds only after an authorised and recorded voluntary decision.
objects.title: Determine and initiate regulatory reporting paths
objects.trigger_or_frequency: When an incident or cyber-threat classification is created or materially revised

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Prohibit automatic routing, preserve the deadline, and escalate channel confirmation to the authorised regulatory liaison.
implementation_rules.statement: Select the current secure channel by competent authority, entity, jurisdiction, event type, and report stage; route Malta major ICT reports and chosen significant-threat notifications through MFSA CRMS in the Licence Holder Portal using the provided template.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Deny transmission, record the access event, and escalate to the submission owner.
implementation_rules.statement: Permit external transmission only to an authenticated actor with the approved submission role and a recorded release decision for the exact package digest and destination.

conditions: The primary competent-authority channel cannot be used.
implementation_rules.failure_handling: Escalate immediately, avoid insecure transmission, and preserve evidence of outage, authority contact, and delivery attempts.
implementation_rules.statement: If the authority channel is unavailable, record technical impossibility, notify the authority through another secure means agreed with it, and resubmit through the primary channel when the authority requires and the channel becomes available.

implementation_rules.failure_handling: Treat delivery as unverified, contact the authority through an approved route, and repeat submission when authorised.
implementation_rules.statement: Retain the transmitted package digest, destination, sender, submission time, authority receipt or response, and any later resubmission linked to the reporting case.

objects.objective: An authorised actor sends each approved reporting package through the competent authority's current secure channel, preserves receipt and package integrity, and uses the agreed secure fallback and resubmission path when required.
objects.title: Authorise and transmit regulatory incident submissions securely
objects.trigger_or_frequency: When a reporting package is ready for external submission or resubmission

evidence_requirements.description: Applicability, request, reference year, incident population, calculation, source, and adjustment reconciliation.
Completed Joint Guidelines Annex and release record for the authority-requested annual estimate.

objects.expected_result: The annual estimate is applicable, complete, period-consistent, mathematically correct, source-reconciled, and ready for authorised submission.
failure_criteria: Request, applicability, reference-year consistency, or reference-year-change approval evidence is missing.
The incident population is incomplete or gross amounts and recoveries are netted or miscalculated.
A value, adjustment, total, or incident reference cannot be reconciled to an approved source.
objects.on_failure: Block report release, correct applicability, population, calculations, or reconciliation, and repeat the complete review.
preconditions: The authority request, applicability assessment, reference-year decision, final incident reports, financial records, calculations, adjustments, and Annex report are available.
procedure: Confirm the request and full-framework non-microenterprise applicability and validate the selected completed reference year.
Reconcile included incidents to current- and prior-year final reports and current-year quantifiable impacts.
Reperform per-incident gross cost and loss and separate recovery calculations, then reconcile aggregate totals.
Trace each value and adjustment to financial statements, supervisory reporting, accounting provisions, or a documented alternative estimate basis.
Confirm the Annex contains totals, per-incident details, final-report references, approvals, and the approved submission route.
objects.title: Verify annual major-incident cost and loss estimates
objects.trigger_or_frequency: Before responding to a competent-authority request and after material corrections to a submitted estimate

evidence_requirements.description: Versioned fall-back and recovery plan for the change.
Results of the required fall-back or recovery verification.

objects.expected_result: The plan is complete, owned, feasible, and verified at the required depth before implementation.
failure_criteria: Required fall-back or recovery information is missing.
A required backup or dependency is unavailable.
Verification fails or does not meet the approved depth.
objects.on_failure: Block implementation, remediate the plan or environment, and repeat the required test.
preconditions: The change has a fall-back and recovery plan with identified owners and dependencies.
procedure: Inspect abort criteria, decision authority, fall-back steps, recovery steps, backups, and restored-service checks.
Confirm the selected verification depth follows the institution's approved risk and criticality rule.
Execute or review the required fall-back test and confirm remediation of failed results.
objects.title: Verify change fall-back and recovery readiness
objects.trigger_or_frequency: Before production implementation and after material fall-back design changes

evidence_requirements.description: Approval of the identified ICT change management process version.
The approved ICT change management protocols reviewed by assurance.

objects.expected_result: Management approval is valid, required protocols are complete, and only the approved process version is effective.
failure_criteria: Management approval is missing or issued by an unauthorised role.
A required protocol area is absent.
The effective process differs from the approved version.
objects.on_failure: Prevent the process version from becoming effective and track governance remediation to closure.
preconditions: The proposed process version and protocols are available for review.
procedure: Confirm the process version has approval from the institution's authorised management role.
Confirm protocols cover intake, classification, assessment, approval, implementation, verification, exceptions, and closure.
Confirm the effective process version matches the approved version.
objects.title: Verify ICT change governance and process approval
objects.trigger_or_frequency: When the ICT change process is established or materially revised

evidence_requirements.description: The complete controlled record of the ICT change lifecycle.
The append-only history of lifecycle transitions and control decisions.

objects.expected_result: The change has one traceable identity and all required gates occur in the permitted order with passing results.
failure_criteria: A stable change identifier or lifecycle history is missing.
Implementation occurs before a required gate passes.
The change closes without post-implementation verification.
objects.on_failure: Block the pending transition where possible, reopen the change when necessary, and repeat verification after remediation.
preconditions: The change system exposes lifecycle states, gate results, approvals, and timestamps.
procedure: Resolve the stable change identifier and read its complete lifecycle history.
Check that assessment, testing, and approval gates passed before implementation.
Check that implementation and post-implementation verification are recorded before closure.
objects.title: Verify controlled ICT change lifecycle gates
objects.trigger_or_frequency: Before production implementation and before change closure

evidence_requirements.description: Approved change plan and transition information.
Record showing distribution of current change details to affected roles.

objects.expected_result: Required planning fields and responsibilities are complete, internally consistent, and communicated before implementation.
failure_criteria: A required role or planning field is missing.
Scope, timeline, or expected outcomes conflict across records.
Required communication is missing or late.
objects.on_failure: Return the change to planning and repeat inspection after records and communication are corrected.
preconditions: The change plan and communication record are available.
procedure: Check that accountable roles, specification, implementation plan, transition design, testing approach, and quality assurance are documented.
Check that purpose, scope, timeline, and expected outcomes are complete.
Check that affected roles received the current change details before implementation.
objects.title: Verify change planning, responsibilities, and communication
objects.trigger_or_frequency: Before implementation approval

evidence_requirements.description: Change record containing stable identities for conflicting roles.
Audit trail for approval attempts and workflow decisions.

objects.expected_result: The approver differs from requester and implementer, and valid approval precedes deployment.
failure_criteria: The approver matches the requester.
The approver matches the implementer.
Approval is missing, rejected, or recorded after deployment.
objects.on_failure: Block approval or deployment, retain the failed attempt, and escalate to the change management owner.
preconditions: Requester, implementer, and approver identities are recorded using stable identity keys.
procedure: Read requester, implementer, and approver identities from the change record.
Compare the approver identity with requester and implementer identities.
Check the approval timestamp and workflow result before deployment.
objects.title: Verify ICT change approval independence
objects.trigger_or_frequency: At approval and before each production deployment

evidence_requirements.description: Assessment of affected ICT security measures and additional safeguards.
Simplified-framework ICT and information security risk assessment for a major change.

objects.expected_result: Security impacts and additional measures are complete and approved; simplified-framework major changes have a documented ICT and information security risk assessment.
failure_criteria: An affected ICT security measure is omitted.
An additional required measure lacks treatment or completion evidence.
A simplified-framework major change lacks the required risk assessment.
objects.on_failure: Block change approval, complete or correct the assessment and treatments, and repeat verification.
preconditions: The change scope, affected assets, existing security measures, and framework branch are identified.
procedure: Check the assessment identifies affected ICT security measures and evaluates changes to their effectiveness.
Check required additional security measures have owners and completion status before implementation.
For the simplified branch, apply approved major-change criteria and confirm a risk assessment exists when the criteria are met.
objects.title: Verify ICT security impact and major-change risk assessment
objects.trigger_or_frequency: Before change approval and whenever change scope materially changes

evidence_requirements.description: Test scope, requirement coverage, execution results, defects, and final disposition for the change.
Approval confirming that security and testing gates passed before production implementation.

objects.expected_result: Security requirement coverage is complete, test depth is justified, all required tests pass, and approval precedes implementation.
failure_criteria: An applicable security requirement lacks a test or accepted treatment.
Test depth does not follow the approved rule.
A required test fails, is missing, or completes after implementation.
objects.on_failure: Block production implementation, remediate failed coverage or results, and repeat verification.
preconditions: Applicable ICT security requirements and change risk classification are recorded.
procedure: Check that each applicable ICT security requirement maps to one or more test cases.
Check that test depth follows the institution's approved risk and criticality rule.
Confirm required tests passed and approval occurred before production implementation.
objects.title: Verify security requirements and tests before production change
objects.trigger_or_frequency: Before production implementation approval

evidence_requirements.description: Complete emergency change record before, during, and after implementation.
Re-evaluation, assessment, omitted-control results, and retrospective approval.

objects.expected_result: Emergency-path use is justified and authorised, safeguards are traceable, and post-implementation review and approval complete on time.
failure_criteria: Emergency-path justification, approval, access record, or audit trail is missing.
Implemented workarounds or patches are not documented and assessed.
Retrospective review or approval exceeds the authorised period.
objects.on_failure: Escalate immediately, restrict emergency access where appropriate, and track review and remediation to closure.
preconditions: The change is classified as emergency and has a complete audit trail.
procedure: Confirm emergency justification, authorised access, approval, and safeguards applied before implementation.
Confirm the final implementation, workarounds, and patches are documented after execution.
Confirm re-evaluation, assessment, omitted controls, and retrospective approval complete within the institution's authorised period.
objects.title: Verify emergency change safeguards and post-implementation review
objects.trigger_or_frequency: During emergency execution and after every emergency change

evidence_requirements.description: Versioned incident or significant-threat criteria assessment and conclusion.
Immutable history of classification submissions and reassessments.

objects.expected_result: The classification is complete, reproducible from current source rules and facts, and preserves every assessment revision.
failure_criteria: A prescribed criterion is omitted or an estimate is presented as an actual value.
An internal severity threshold replaces or alters a legal major-incident condition.
The conclusion cannot be reproduced or prior assessment history is missing.
objects.on_failure: Mark the classification unverified, apply conservative escalation, correct the assessment, and repeat review.
preconditions: The current legal criteria and thresholds, case facts, estimates, calculations, and classification history are available.
procedure: Confirm every prescribed criterion has a value, justified estimate, or explicit unavailable status.
Recalculate the major-incident result using the critical-service condition and prescribed combination rule.
For a significant cyber threat, confirm all function or party, probability, and hypothetical materiality conditions are evidenced.
Confirm source-rule version, assessor, timestamps, changes, and prior conclusions are retained.
objects.title: Verify incident and significant-threat classification
objects.trigger_or_frequency: At each classification conclusion and after material input changes

evidence_requirements.description: Applicable communication plan, trigger assessment, recipients, content approval, and external-obligation evaluation.
Trace of internal, client, public, and authority communications issued for the case.

objects.expected_result: Every triggered communication is authorised, complete, timely, consistent with case facts, and traceable to recipients and delivery evidence.
failure_criteria: A required internal escalation, client communication, or parallel notification is missing or overdue.
External content was issued by an unauthorised role or conflicts with verified incident facts.
A potentially applicable obligation lacks a documented decision.
objects.on_failure: Escalate immediately, correct or issue the communication through an approved channel, record impact, and repeat verification.
preconditions: The incident classification, impact assessment, communication plan, escalation matrix, client assessment, and external obligation register are available.
procedure: Confirm required senior-management and management-body escalations were complete and timely.
Confirm crisis and public communications used authorised roles, content, recipients, and channels.
Confirm affected-client and significant-threat protection communications match the documented trigger and contain required mitigation information.
Reconcile the case against the external notification register and confirm every parallel obligation has an outcome.
objects.title: Verify incident escalation and stakeholder communications
objects.trigger_or_frequency: When a communication obligation is triggered and before communication work is closed

evidence_requirements.description: Versioned monitoring, logging, threshold, ownership, and coverage configuration used by the test.
Results and alert traces for each representative detection scenario.

objects.expected_result: Required inputs and assets are covered, representative indicators create complete alerts, and failed or inconclusive detection enters a controlled fallback path.
failure_criteria: A required input, critical asset, or simplified-framework event category lacks effective monitoring or logging.
A representative indicator does not create a timely, prioritised, traceable alert.
Out-of-hours or manual fallback processing fails.
objects.on_failure: Record the control gap, apply compensating monitoring, prioritise critical coverage, remediate, and repeat the failed test.
preconditions: The asset inventory, critical-function mapping, monitoring coverage, logging standard, thresholds, and escalation routes are available.
procedure: Map required monitoring inputs and simplified-framework log categories to covered assets and identify gaps.
Inject or replay representative malicious activity, data-loss, availability, operational-impact, vulnerability, user-report, and third-party indicators.
Confirm each applicable indicator is logged, triaged, prioritised, linked to an incident case, and sent to the responsible role inside and outside working hours.
Confirm failures and inconclusive automated decisions trigger manual triage and preserve source data.
objects.title: Test incident detection, logging, triage, and alerting
objects.trigger_or_frequency: At the approved monitoring-test frequency and after material monitoring changes

evidence_requirements.description: The complete governed record for the event, threat, or payment-related incident.
Approved policy, responsibility map, contacts, record protection, and retention decision applicable to the case.

objects.expected_result: The case is governed, complete, protected, traceable, and subject to an approved evidence-retention outcome.
failure_criteria: An in-scope event lacks a stable case, owner, or applicable process path.
Required chronology or root-cause follow-up data is missing or can be altered without trace.
Evidence access, integrity, retention, or disposal conflicts with the approved controls.
objects.on_failure: Prevent closure or disposal, preserve available evidence, escalate the gap, remediate it, and repeat verification.
preconditions: The incident policy, role map, case record, evidence inventory, and retention schedule are available.
procedure: Confirm the case scope includes applicable ICT, threat, and payment-event paths and has one stable identifier.
Confirm activated roles, contacts, chronology, decisions, actions, and root-cause follow-up are complete.
Inspect access and integrity controls for the record and linked evidence.
Confirm the applied retention outcome follows the approved schedule, criticality basis, recurring-assessment need, and legal hold status.
objects.title: Verify incident governance, records, and evidence handling
objects.trigger_or_frequency: Before case closure and when the incident policy, role map, record controls, or retention schedule changes

evidence_requirements.description: Chronology of containment, recovery, impact estimates, material updates, and decisions.
Results for functionality, security, integrity, and temporary-treatment checks before restoration.

objects.expected_result: Containment is controlled, estimates are current, and service is restored only after all approved operational and security criteria pass.
failure_criteria: Required containment or recovery actions are missing, unsuitable, or untraceable.
Impact information is stale or mixes estimated and actual values.
Service restoration is declared with a failed or unevaluated security, integrity, or functionality criterion.
objects.on_failure: Keep or return the service to a restricted state, escalate the failed criterion, continue recovery, and repeat verification.
preconditions: The incident case, applicable playbook, affected services, current impact estimate, and restoration criteria are available.
procedure: Confirm the selected containment and recovery arrangements match the recorded incident facts and were activated with timestamps.
Check impact, damage, loss, estimate status, and material updates are current and traceable.
Test service functionality, security, data integrity, and temporary risk treatments against the approved restoration criteria.
Confirm material response and recovery changes reached communication and reporting owners.
objects.title: Verify incident containment and secure restoration
objects.trigger_or_frequency: During response and before declaring affected services restored

evidence_requirements.description: Monthly recurring-incident population, grouping, calculations, trends, and resulting actions.
Annual incident-derived findings and recommendations delivered by senior ICT staff to the management body.

objects.expected_result: Monthly recurring assessments are complete and reproducible, trends drive action, and annual findings reach the management body with recorded outcomes.
failure_criteria: The monthly population or six-month grouping is incomplete.
A collectively major group lacks a reporting assessment.
Trend dimensions, recommendations, management-body delivery, or resulting decisions are missing.
objects.on_failure: Complete the missing assessment or report, escalate potentially reportable groups immediately, and repeat verification.
preconditions: The complete incident population, root-cause links, classification data, trend output, and management reporting calendar are available.
procedure: Reconcile the monthly population and identify all qualifying two-or-more incident groups in the six-month lookback period.
Reperform the aggregate major-incident calculation for each qualifying group and trace any major result to reporting assessment.
Confirm significant and recurring pattern analysis covers the prescribed dimensions and links findings to action.
Confirm senior ICT staff provided complete findings and recommendations to the management body within the annual cycle and retained its decisions.
objects.title: Verify recurring-incident analysis and management reporting
objects.trigger_or_frequency: After each monthly assessment and each annual management-body report

evidence_requirements.description: Reporting arrangement, accountability terms, third-party identity, and start or end notices to the authority.
Eligibility, population, permission, aggregate package, and any institution-specific authority response.

objects.expected_result: Delegation, aggregation, recurring populations, and individual follow-up satisfy every condition and preserve complete EMI accountability.
failure_criteria: Responsibility is transferred or an authority notice is missing, incomplete, or late.
Any aggregation condition, institution classification, authority permission, or constituent incident link is missing.
An authority-requested individual report is absent or incomplete.
objects.on_failure: Prevent or correct the submission, assume direct reporting control where needed, notify the authority, and repeat verification.
preconditions: The outsourcing arrangement, authority notices, institution classifications, aggregation assessment, submissions, and authority requests are available.
procedure: Confirm the arrangement preserves EMI accountability and authority notices contain required third-party details and timing.
Reperform every third-party aggregation condition, including authority permission, and reconcile all covered institutions.
For recurring-incident aggregation, reconcile every constituent incident to the monthly assessment and collective major classification.
Confirm every authority request for institution-specific impact after aggregation has a complete individual response.
objects.title: Verify outsourced and aggregated incident reporting
