objects.trigger_or_frequency: Before a first outsourced submission, each aggregated submission, and closure of an outsourcing arrangement or authority request

evidence_requirements.description: Root-cause, procedure, effectiveness, and lesson review for the incident.
Traceability from findings to risk, framework, control, and corrective-action updates.

objects.expected_result: The review is evidence-based, complete for the applicable framework, and every finding has a traceable risk, control, or corrective-action outcome.
failure_criteria: Root causes or a required effectiveness area are missing or unsupported.
A finding lacks an owner, due date, and treatment outcome.
Required full- or simplified-framework review content is absent.
objects.on_failure: Keep the review open, assign remediation, escalate overdue items, and repeat assurance before closure.
preconditions: The complete incident record, response chronology, classification, root-cause analysis, framework branch, risks, controls, and corrective actions are available.
procedure: Confirm the review covers causes, procedure adherence, response effectiveness, impact assessment, forensics where appropriate, escalation, communication, containment, and recovery.
Trace each supported finding to an owned corrective action, risk update, control update, or justified no-action decision.
Confirm the applicable full- or simplified-framework review requirements and report content are complete.
Confirm the review report can be supplied to the competent authority when required.
objects.title: Verify post-incident review and learning
objects.trigger_or_frequency: Before closing each required post-incident and framework review

evidence_requirements.description: Identity of the official template and instructions applied to the package.
Field-level validation and reconciliation result for the exact reporting package.

objects.expected_result: The exact package passes current template, field, format, consistency, accuracy, estimate, and version-history checks.
failure_criteria: The template identity or official origin cannot be verified.
A required or conditionally required field is missing, malformed, inaccurate, or inconsistent.
An estimate is unlabelled, an actual value is not updated, or a prior package version is lost.
objects.on_failure: Block package release, record field-level defects, correct the package under version control, and repeat the complete validation.
preconditions: The official template metadata, candidate package, incident record, classification, prior submissions, recovery record, and financial data are available.
procedure: Verify the template source, retrieval time, version or label, and SHA-256 digest against the applicable official channel.
Apply all general and stage-specific required-field, format, and conditional rules to the package.
Reconcile identifiers, times, classification, impacts, costs, recoveries, currency, and status with source records and prior stages.
Confirm estimates and unavailable values are labelled and prior package versions remain preserved.
objects.title: Verify regulatory report content and template integrity
objects.trigger_or_frequency: Before authorising each external incident report or significant-threat notification

evidence_requirements.description: Calculated deadlines, source timestamps, calendar inputs, exceptions, alerts, and completion outcomes.
Stage sequence, combined submission, delay, update, and reclassification decisions for the reporting case.

objects.expected_result: Every stage, deadline, exception, delay, update, and reclassification is correctly calculated, actioned, and evidenced.
failure_criteria: A deadline is miscalculated, missed without timely delay notice, or based on an unsupported extension.
Report stages are missing, out of order, combined without eligibility, or finalised before required inputs are available.
A required update or reclassification notification is absent.
objects.on_failure: Escalate immediately, notify the authority where required, correct the ledger or submission, and repeat verification.
preconditions: Awareness, classification, report, update, recovery, root-cause, calendar, authority-decision, and submission timestamps are available.
procedure: Recalculate initial, intermediate, and final deadlines from recorded source timestamps and compare them with the deadline ledger.
Confirm stage order, update triggers, final-report readiness, and any combined-stage submission satisfy all prescribed conditions.
Reperform every weekend or bank-holiday extension decision and confirm excluded stages or authority decisions were applied.
Confirm threatened delays were notified by the applicable deadline with reasons and any reclassification followed the prescribed path.
objects.title: Verify regulatory report stages and deadlines
objects.trigger_or_frequency: Before each reporting deadline, after each submission, and when classification or recovery status changes

evidence_requirements.description: Classification-trigger, payment-event route, authority, and mandatory or voluntary reporting outcome.
Authorised decision to submit or decline a significant-cyber-threat notification.

objects.expected_result: Mandatory, payment-event, and voluntary paths are selected through their distinct rules and every outcome is complete and traceable.
failure_criteria: A major classification did not initiate reporting immediately or was held for optional approval.
A payment-related event lacks a Chapter III reporting assessment.
A significant-threat notification lacks an authorised voluntary decision or a reporting outcome lacks case linkage.
objects.on_failure: Open or correct the reporting workflow immediately, preserve original timestamps, escalate the defect, and repeat verification.
preconditions: The classification, event type, authority routing register, voluntary-decision record, and reporting-case linkage are available.
procedure: Confirm every verified major ICT-related incident immediately created a mandatory reporting workflow and deadline ledger without an optional approval dependency.
Confirm each payment-related operational or security incident was routed through the applicable Chapter III assessment, including non-ICT events.
Confirm a significant-threat notification exists only after an authorised relevance and voluntary-notification decision.
Trace the reporting workflow to the source case, classification revision, authority, trigger, decision basis, and deadlines.
objects.title: Verify regulatory reporting initiation decisions
objects.trigger_or_frequency: After a major-incident or significant-threat classification and before closing reportability assessment

evidence_requirements.description: Approved destination, channel, actor, access decision, and exact package identity.
Transmission, authority receipt, fallback, and resubmission evidence for the exact package.

objects.expected_result: The approved package reaches the correct authority through an authorised secure path with intact content and a complete receipt or fallback trail.
failure_criteria: The channel, destination, actor, or package differs from the approved submission data.
Delivery lacks a receipt or verified authority response and no follow-up exists.
Fallback transmission is insecure, unagreed, unsupported by technical-impossibility evidence, or lacks required resubmission.
objects.on_failure: Treat delivery as unverified, escalate immediately, contact the authority through an approved route, and resubmit when authorised.
preconditions: The approved package, package digest, authority route, access policy, submission actor, channel status, and authority responses are available.
procedure: Confirm the selected channel matches the authority, jurisdiction, entity, event type, and report stage, including applicable MFSA CRMS routes.
Confirm the authenticated sender held the approved role and release decision for the exact package and destination.
